addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text **moves** here
(never copied; one home per text). The picked-up task is a
`###` heading; a multi-cycle program adds one level, where the
program is the `###` and its current stage a `####` (headings
give the current work durable anchors, which numbered Todo
entries can't). The problem overview is followed by the
"plan", a bulleted list of the development "ladder". Each
rung is prepended with its commit reference, a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then
backfilled to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as
the chores As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

### Refactor: typed jj facade -> jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", ...)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init: stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

Program ladder in **straight trunk order**, one bullet per
commit that lands on the branch, so reading it top to bottom
is reading `git log --first-parent`. `refactor:` entries are
the program's rungs, one per cycle (adjacent stages
consolidated 2026-07-24; titles are the anticipated close-out
titles; unshipped versions are provisional, since jj-lib may
split into two cycles). `docs:` entries are interludes that
sit between cycles and belong to no rung. Every shipped ref
points at a close-out commit on `refactor-vc-x1`, treated as
permanent: the branch is long-lived and lands on main
merge-only, never rebased.

The order is load-bearing: a
trapezoid's `<base>` is the parent of its own first rung, not
the previous close-out, so 0.78.0 bases on 0.77.4. Taking the
close-out instead swallows the interludes into the merge's
ladder side, which already bit at 0.76.0, whose base was the
0.75.1 interlude. See
[the recipe](notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe).

- [[1]] 0.73.0 refactor: DRY jj facade (done)

152	    by repo path, has-a and never is-a, because an
153	    invocation touches 0..N repos and repo-less commands
154	    (`version`) must not open one; verbs become session
155	    methods; the one-shot facade fns stay as wrappers for
156	    context-less callers
157	  - one op per verb stays: sharing a transaction across
158	    stages would change the op-log shape that push re-run
159	    and sync revert rely on
160	  - per-verb opens are the lifted subprocess lifecycle made
161	    visible, not a regression; this rung is the improvement
162	    over the spawned form, and push / squash-push / sync are
163	    its consumers today
164	  - ordered before the retry so the retry lands on the final
165	    frame, though it fits either shape

167	  - renumbered from `-7` by the session insert
168	  - bugs.md #1, with the `git init --bare` to gix rider
169	  - the retry classifies by error variant rather than
170	    substring, which is the real win: `SpawnInPath` and
171	    `UnsupportedGitOption` are never retryable, and treating
172	    the whole `Subprocess` arm as retryable would loop
173	    forever on a missing git binary

176	##### Decisions at cycle open
177	
178	- **All three pieces**, decided 2026-07-30: jj-lib for reads,
179	  jj-lib for mutations, and the index-lock retry that is the
180	  headline prize. The 2026-07-29 session ended undecided
181	  between this and deferring mutations.
182	- **What changed is the coexistence objection, not the
183	  evidence.** The risk section concluded the coupling was
184	  "unenforceable, probably fine" because a `jj --version`
185	  check cannot answer whether two versions are compatible.
186	  That evaluates it as a compatibility oracle. As a guard on
187	  our own writes it fits the actual risk direction: the
188	  dangerous case is an old jj reading an op written by a
189	  newer jj-lib, and refusing to write on a mismatch closes
190	  exactly that. The safe direction, a newer jj reading our
191	  older op, is something jj must support anyway, since the
192	  user's own older jj wrote into that repo first.
193	  - **Half superseded 2026-07-31.** The conclusion stands;
194	    the "safe direction" sentence does not. See
195	    [why equality, and why at startup](#why-equality-and-why-at-startup).
196	    Kept as written because this section records what was

40	   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.

42	   complete.
43	6. Write the description: <=72-col conventional title, prose body (work repo: file-by-file,
44	   opening with the version-bump bullet). See
45	   [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
46	7. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
47	   explicitly includes it.

1	# Code conventions
2	
3	Conventions for source code. Read this before writing code. The Rust-specific sections apply
4	wherever the medium is a Rust crate (see [custom.md](../custom.md) for the project's medium).
5	
6	Universal file, pinned to vc-x1-work-repo-template; do not edit here. Project overrides go in
7	[custom.md](../custom.md).
8	
9	## Line width
10	
11	Source lines, including doc comments and inline comments, wrap at <=100 cols (rustfmt's
12	default `max_width`; the per-commit flow's `cargo fmt` enforces it for code, and the same limit
13	applies to the comment text it doesn't reflow).
14	
15	## Doc comments on every file, function, and method
16	
17	Every `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every function and method must have
18	a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief: one sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline
19	is that the comment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the
20	[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) shape (intro + bullets).
21	
22	This is a deliberate override of the generic "write no comments" default that applies to
23	inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the module / item surface are expected; inline
24	explanatory comments inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a
25	non-obvious WHY.
26	
27	**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows
28	by default and collapses bullets into running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on
29	any field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- ...` lands on its own line in the rendered
30	help.
31	
32	## `// OK: ...` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)
33	
34	The default in non-test code is to **not** use `.unwrap()`, `.expect(...)`, or the
35	`.unwrap_or*(...)` siblings. Prefer a shape that doesn't need them (`match`, `if let`, slice
36	patterns, infallible-by-construction APIs), which is usually also the clearer code. This is a
37	lean, not a ban: some sites are legitimately best expressed with one. Two kinds of risk, both
38	in scope:
39	
40	- `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`: a panic path.
41	- `.unwrap_or(...)` / `.unwrap_or_default()` / `.unwrap_or_else(...)`: no panic, but a
42	  silently substituted value that can hide a wrong result.
43	
44	When one is used, three obligations attach:
45	
46	- A trailing `// OK: ...` comment justifying why the call is acceptable:
47	  - `// OK: <specific reason>`: document the real precondition, invariant, or domain reason.
48	    Preferred whenever the reason isn't self-evident.
49	  - `// OK: obvious`: the default is self-evident from context (e.g.
50	    `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("")`, where an empty desc gives an empty title).
51	  - Bare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment). Abbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are
52	    not used because they require a decoder ring for readers seeing the code out of context.
53	- **Alert the user in conversation** when introducing one, so the site gets reviewed and
54	  appropriate uses are learned. Don't let it ride in silently on a larger diff.
55	- For `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`, an `#[allow(...)]` at the site, because Rust projects
56	  enable the project-wide lints in `Cargo.toml`:
57	
58	  ```toml
59	  [lints.clippy]
60	  unwrap_used = "warn"
61	  expect_used = "warn"
62	  ```
63	
64	  Every panicking site is then opt-in and visible in the diff; clippy (in the per-commit flow)
65	  catches any that slip through. The `_or*` siblings have no clippy lint; they are covered by
66	  the comment convention and the conversational alert. (The vc-x1-work-repo-template's
67	  `CargoRust.toml` seeds a base `Cargo.toml` with this section already in place.)
68	
69	```rust
70	let max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent
71	let first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("");  // OK: obvious
72	
73	match matches.len() {
74	    1 => {
75	        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
76	        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1
77	        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))
78	    }
79	    // ...
80	}
81	```
82	
83	Tests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt, since panicking on setup failure is the correct test
84	behavior.

# Code conventions

Conventions for source code. Read this before writing code. The Rust-specific sections apply
wherever the medium is a Rust crate (see [custom.md](../custom.md) for the project's medium).

Universal file, pinned to vc-x1-work-repo-template; do not edit here. Project overrides go in
[custom.md](../custom.md).

## Line width

Source lines, including doc comments and inline comments, wrap at <=100 cols (rustfmt's
default `max_width`; the per-commit flow's `cargo fmt` enforces it for code, and the same limit
applies to the comment text it doesn't reflow).

## Doc comments on every file, function, and method

Every `.rs` file must begin with a `//!` module docstring. Every function and method must have
a `///` doc comment. Keep them brief: one sentence of purpose is often enough; the discipline
is that the comment exists, not that it be long. Doc comments follow the
[Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) shape (intro + bullets).

This is a deliberate override of the generic "write no comments" default that applies to
inline `//` comments. Doc comments on the module / item surface are expected; inline
explanatory comments inside function bodies remain discouraged unless they capture a
non-obvious WHY.

**Clap-derive args:** doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help` output. Clap reflows
by default and collapses bullets into running prose. Add `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, ...)]` on
any field whose doc comment uses bullets so each `- ...` lands on its own line in the rendered
help.

## `// OK: ...` comments on `unwrap*` calls (Rust)

The default in non-test code is to **not** use `.unwrap()`, `.expect(...)`, or the
`.unwrap_or*(...)` siblings. Prefer a shape that doesn't need them (`match`, `if let`, slice
patterns, infallible-by-construction APIs), which is usually also the clearer code. This is a
lean, not a ban: some sites are legitimately best expressed with one. Two kinds of risk, both
in scope:

- `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`: a panic path.
- `.unwrap_or(...)` / `.unwrap_or_default()` / `.unwrap_or_else(...)`: no panic, but a
  silently substituted value that can hide a wrong result.

When one is used, three obligations attach:

- A trailing `// OK: ...` comment justifying why the call is acceptable:
  - `// OK: <specific reason>`: document the real precondition, invariant, or domain reason.
    Preferred whenever the reason isn't self-evident.
  - `// OK: obvious`: the default is self-evident from context (e.g.
    `desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("")`, where an empty desc gives an empty title).
  - Bare `// OK` is not used (reads like a truncated comment). Abbreviations (e.g. `SE`) are
    not used because they require a decoder ring for readers seeing the code out of context.
- **Alert the user in conversation** when introducing one, so the site gets reviewed and
  appropriate uses are learned. Don't let it ride in silently on a larger diff.
- For `.unwrap()` / `.expect(...)`, an `#[allow(...)]` at the site, because Rust projects
  enable the project-wide lints in `Cargo.toml`:

  ```toml
  [lints.clippy]
  unwrap_used = "warn"
  expect_used = "warn"
  ```

  Every panicking site is then opt-in and visible in the diff; clippy (in the per-commit flow)
  catches any that slip through. The `_or*` siblings have no clippy lint; they are covered by
  the comment convention and the conversational alert. (The vc-x1-work-repo-template's
  `CargoRust.toml` seeds a base `Cargo.toml` with this section already in place.)

```rust
let max = stderr_level.unwrap_or(LevelFilter::Info); // OK: default verbosity when -v/-vv absent
let first_line = desc.lines().next().unwrap_or("");  // OK: obvious

match matches.len() {
    1 => {
        #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
        // OK: `1 =>` arm guarantees matches.len() == 1
        Ok(TitleMatch::One(matches.into_iter().next().unwrap()))
    }
    // ...
}
```

Tests (`#[cfg(test)]`) are exempt, since panicking on setup failure is the correct test
behavior.

1	//! The `sync` subcommand: fetch + classify + rebase / fast-forward
2	//! a workspace's repos against their remotes, then reposition `@`
3	//! onto the synced bookmark.
4	//!
5	//! `--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot
6	//! repo is a linear journal on `main` by design, so every
7	//! per-repo step (tracking preflight, classify, act, reposition)
8	//! resolves its bookmark via `repo_bookmark`, which pins the
9	//! bot repo to `main`.
10	//!
11	//! Sync is a single atomic operation — verify-then-act happens
12	//! inside one invocation against one fetch snapshot (a separate
13	//! check-then-apply pair of runs would race the remote). The
14	//! hidden deprecated `--check` flag preserves the old verify-only
15	//! mode for `push`'s preflight until that is rewired in-process.

38	/// Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes.
39	///
40	/// One atomic operation: fetch, classify, fast-forward / rebase the
41	/// bookmark as needed, then reposition `@` onto it. On any failure
42	/// the starting state of every repo is restored via `jj op restore`.
43	///
44	/// Repo set is resolved from `-R/--repo` + `--scope`:
45	///
46	/// - `-R PATH` — workspace root, or a single repo to sync alone.
47	/// - `--scope=work|bot|work,bot` — keyword role selection,
48	///   resolved via the workspace root's `.vc-config.toml`.
49	/// - Neither — workspace-default scope:
50	///   - dual workspace (`.vc-config.toml` with `bot`) → `work,bot`
51	///   - single-repo workspace (`.vc-config.toml`, no `bot`) → `work`
52	///   - POR (no `.vc-config.toml`) → cwd
53	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
54	pub struct SyncArgs {
55	    /// Verify only — fetch + classify; error if any repo needs
56	    /// action; no bookmark move, no `@` reposition.
57	    ///
58	    /// Deprecated and hidden: kept solely for `push`'s preflight
59	    /// shell-out until that is rewired in-process (see the
60	    /// `TODO.md` sync follow-up). Note the fetch still
61	    /// auto-fast-forwards a tracked bookmark — this mode was never
62	    /// fully read-only.
63	    #[arg(long, hide = true)]
64	    pub check: bool,
65	
66	    /// Suppress all informational output (exit code signals result)
67	    #[arg(short, long)]
68	    pub quiet: bool,
69	
70	    /// Bookmark to sync in the work repo. The session (bot) repo
71	    /// is a linear journal and always syncs `main`, regardless.
72	    #[arg(long, default_value = "main")]
73	    pub bookmark: String,
74	
75	    /// Remote to sync against
76	    #[arg(long, default_value = "origin")]
77	    pub remote: String,
78	
79	    /// Rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced bookmark without asking.
80	    ///
81	    /// After a successful sync, `@` is repositioned onto the synced
82	    /// bookmark. When the work repo's `@` carries changes it normally
83	    /// asks before rebasing; `--rebase` answers yes up front for
84	    /// non-interactive use. Ignored for the bot repo (which
85	    /// always `jj new main`).
86	    #[arg(long)]
87	    pub rebase: bool,
88	
89	    /// Workspace root, or a single jj repo to sync on its own.
90	    ///
91	    /// - `-R PATH` alone — sync just the repo at PATH.
92	    /// - `-R PATH -s ROLES` — use PATH as the workspace root and
93	    ///   sync the named side(s).
94	    #[arg(short = 'R', long = "repo", value_name = "PATH", verbatim_doc_comment)]
95	    pub repo: Option<PathBuf>,
96	
97	    /// Which repo(s) of the workspace to sync.
98	    ///
99	    /// `SCOPE=work|bot|work,bot`:
100	    ///
101	    /// - `work` — sync only the work repo.
102	    /// - `bot` — sync only the bot repo (errors if no bot repo
103	    ///   is configured).
104	    /// - `work,bot` — sync both repos.
105	    ///
106	    /// Composes with `-R` as the workspace root. Default depends
107	    /// on workspace state: dual workspace → `work,bot`;
108	    /// single-repo workspace or POR → `work`.
109	    #[arg(
110	        short = 's',
111	        long,
112	        value_name = "SCOPE",
113	        value_parser = parse_scope,
114	        verbatim_doc_comment
115	    )]
116	    pub scope: Option<Scope>,
117	}

177	/// Resolve a `-R`/`--scope` pair into a concrete repo list.
178	///
179	/// `-R` and `--scope` compose:
180	///
181	/// - neither — workspace-default scope against the discovered root.
182	/// - `-R PATH` alone — just that repo.
183	/// - `-s ROLES` alone — roles against the discovered workspace root.
184	/// - `-R PATH -s ROLES` — roles against `PATH` as the workspace root.
185	///
186	/// `pub(crate)` — shared by `sync` and `revert`, which must resolve
187	/// the same invocation shape to the same repos.
188	pub(crate) fn resolve_repos(
189	    repo: &Option<PathBuf>,
190	    scope: &Option<Scope>,
191	) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
192	    match (repo, scope) {
193	        (None, None) => {
194	            let root = find_workspace_root();
195	            scope_to_repos(&default_scope(root.as_deref()), root.as_deref())
196	        }
197	        (Some(p), None) => Ok(vec![p.clone()]),
198	        (None, Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, find_workspace_root().as_deref()),
199	        (Some(p), Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, Some(p)),
200	    }
201	}

203	/// Relationship between a local bookmark and its remote counterpart.
204	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
205	pub enum State {
206	    /// Local and remote point at the same commit.
207	    UpToDate,
208	    /// Local is a strict ancestor of remote — fast-forward possible.
209	    Behind { local: String, remote: String },
210	    /// Remote is a strict ancestor of local — nothing to pull in.
211	    Ahead { local: String, remote: String },
212	    /// Neither is an ancestor of the other — needs rebase.
213	    Diverged { local: String, remote: String },
214	    /// The bookmark has no `@<remote>` counterpart.
215	    NoRemote,
216	}

219	#[derive(Debug)]

221	    path: PathBuf,
222	    #[allow(dead_code)]
223	    op_id: String,
224	    state: State,

227	/// CLI entry point for the `sync` subcommand.
228	///
229	/// Thin wrapper over `sync_repos` that resolves `--scope` into a
230	/// concrete repo list (falling back to the workspace-default
231	/// scope) and forwards the rest. Tests call `sync_repos` directly
232	/// with absolute fixture paths. `ctx` is unused today — present
233	/// for the uniform subcommand-layer signature.
234	///
235	/// When `--quiet` is set, the global log filter is temporarily
236	/// clamped to `Warn` for the duration of the call and restored on
237	/// return, so `info!` calls throughout sync (plus any
238	/// subprocess-stderr routed through `common::run`) go dark. Errors
239	/// still surface at `Warn` / `Error` so script callers don't lose
240	/// diagnostics.
241	pub fn sync(_ctx: &Context, params: &SyncParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
242	    let repos = resolve_repos(&params.repo, &params.scope)?;
243	    if params.quiet {
244	        let prev = log::max_level();
245	        log::set_max_level(LevelFilter::Warn);
246	        let result = sync_repos(&repos, params);
247	        log::set_max_level(prev);
248	        result
249	    } else {
250	        sync_repos(&repos, params)
251	    }
252	}

254	/// Sync the given repos against their remotes.
255	///
256	/// Orchestrates the full flow: pre-flight clean-check on every repo,
257	/// snapshot each repo's current op id (persisted to
258	/// `.vc-x1/sync-state.toml` per repo), then hand off to `run_plan`
259	/// for fetch + classify + act, then reposition `@`.
260	///
261	/// **Stop-on-error**: a failure leaves every repo exactly where the
262	/// failing step stopped so the user can inspect what happened —
263	/// nothing is auto-reverted. The error report names each repo's
264	/// pre-sync op id and points at `vc-x1 revert`, which consumes the
265	/// persisted snapshots. On full success the snapshots are cleared
266	/// (a stale file must not become a revert target later).
267	///
268	/// Paths may be relative (resolved against the process cwd) or
269	/// absolute. Tests use absolute tempdir paths to avoid cwd dependence
270	/// under parallel `cargo test`.
271	pub fn sync_repos(
272	    repos: &[PathBuf],
273	    params: &SyncParams,
274	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
275	    debug!(
276	        "sync: enter (check={}, bookmark={}, remote={})",
277	        params.check, params.bookmark, params.remote
278	    );
279	
280	    // Preflight: verify bookmark tracking on every repo before any
281	    // fetch/rebase. Implements "Non-tracking-remote bookmark detection"
282	    // — design at:
283	    //   https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-06.md#non-tracking-remote-bookmark-detection-design
284	    for repo in repos {
285	        let bookmark = repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark);
286	        if bookmark != params.bookmark {
287	            info!(
288	                "{}: bot repo — syncing 'main' ('{}' is a work repo bookmark)",
289	                repo.display(),
290	                params.bookmark
291	            );
292	        }
293	        crate::common::verify_tracking(repo, bookmark)?;
294	    }
295	
296	    let mut snapshots: Vec<(PathBuf, String)> = Vec::new();
297	    for repo in repos {
298	        let op_id = current_op_id(repo)?;
299	        debug!("{}: op snapshot = {op_id}", repo.display());
300	        state::save(
301	            repo,
302	            &op_id,
303	            repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark),
304	            &params.remote,
305	        )?;
306	        snapshots.push((repo.clone(), op_id));
307	    }
308	
309	    // Run the plan, then reposition `@` onto the freshly-synced
310	    // bookmark (skipped in deprecated verify-only mode). Both live
311	    // inside the same stop-on-error region: any failure falls
312	    // through to the report below with state left in place.
313	    let result = run_plan(&snapshots, params).and_then(|()| {
314	        if !params.check {
315	            for (repo, _) in &snapshots {
316	                reposition_at(repo, repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark), params)?;
317	            }
318	        }
319	        Ok(())
320	    });
321	
322	    if let Err(e) = &result {
323	        warn!("sync failed: {e}");
324	        warn!("stopping — state left as-is for inspection (no auto-revert)");
325	        warn!("pre-sync op snapshot per repo:");
326	        for (repo, op_id) in &snapshots {
327	            warn!("  {}: op {op_id}", repo.display());
328	        }
329	        warn!("undo with `vc-x1 revert`, or per repo: jj op restore <op> -R <repo>");
330	        debug!("sync: exit");
331	        return result;
332	    }
333	
334	    // Full success — the snapshots are no longer revert targets.
335	    for (repo, _) in &snapshots {
336	        state::clear(repo)?;
337	    }
338	
339	    debug!("sync: exit");
340	    Ok(())
341	}

343	/// Clean-case summary tail ("<N> repo(s) …" prefixed at the emit
344	/// site). Shared with main.rs's `long_about` so the documented
345	/// output shape can't drift from the emitted one.
346	pub const UP_TO_DATE_MSG: &str = "up to date, nothing to sync";
347	
348	/// Fetch and classify each repo, then act (or not, in verify-only).
349	///
350	/// Returns `Err` on the first failure so the caller can stop and
351	/// report; partial progress across repos is left in place for
352	/// inspection (see `sync_repos`).
353	fn run_plan(
354	    snapshots: &[(PathBuf, String)],
355	    params: &SyncParams,
356	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
357	    // Phase 1 — fetch + classify silently.
358	    //
359	    // Each repo's fetch stderr is captured (rather than streamed to
360	    // `info!` via `common::run`) so we can decide after classification
361	    // whether to surface it. `jj git fetch`'s routine "Nothing
362	    // changed." chatter is the main thing we're suppressing here —
363	    // if nothing needs action, the user shouldn't see it.
364	    let mut fetched: Vec<(PathBuf, Vec<String>)> = Vec::new();
365	    let mut ctxs: Vec<RepoCtx> = Vec::new();
366	    for (repo, op_id) in snapshots {
367	        let lines = fetch_silent(repo, &params.remote)?;
368	        fetched.push((repo.clone(), lines));
369	        let state = classify(repo, repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark), &params.remote)?;
370	        ctxs.push(RepoCtx {
371	            path: repo.clone(),
372	            op_id: op_id.clone(),
373	            state,
374	        });
375	    }
376	
377	    let any_action_needed = ctxs
378	        .iter()
379	        .any(|c| matches!(c.state, State::Behind { .. } | State::Diverged { .. }));
380	
381	    // Phase 2 — emit status. `--quiet` is enforced globally via the
382	    // log-level clamp in `sync()`, so these `info!` calls are already
383	    // suppressed in scripts; we just shape the output here.
384	    if !any_action_needed {
385	        let n = ctxs.len();
386	        let noun = if n == 1 { "repo is" } else { "repos are" };
387	        info!("sync: {n} {noun} {UP_TO_DATE_MSG}");
388	    } else {
389	        for (repo, lines) in &fetched {
390	            info!("{}: fetch {}", repo.display(), params.remote);
391	            for line in lines {
392	                info!("{line}");
393	            }
394	        }
395	        for ctx in &ctxs {
396	            log_state(&ctx.path, &ctx.state);
397	        }
398	    }
399	
400	    // Phase 3 — act (subprocess output streams through as usual).
401	    // `act_on_state` short-circuits in deprecated verify-only mode,
402	    // making it a true no-op here. Repositioning `@` onto the synced
403	    // bookmark happens after `run_plan` returns (see `sync_repos`),
404	    // outside the revert region.
405	    for ctx in &ctxs {
406	        act_on_state(ctx, params)?;
407	    }
408	
409	    // Phase 4 — verify-only mode is fatal when action would be
410	    // needed. The normal sync ran the action above and is done.
411	    if params.check && any_action_needed {
412	        let n_action = ctxs
413	            .iter()
414	            .filter(|c| matches!(c.state, State::Behind { .. } | State::Diverged { .. }))
415	            .count();
416	        let noun = if n_action == 1 { "repo" } else { "repos" };
417	        return Err(format!(
418	            "sync: {n_action} {noun} need action (see above) — \
419	             resolve with `vc-x1 sync` and re-run"
420	        )
421	        .into());
422	    }
423	    Ok(())
424	}

426	/// Fetch `repo` from `remote` without streaming chatter to `info!`.

428	/// The facade's in-process fetch returns one line per changed
429	/// remote bookmark; the caller decides whether to surface them
430	/// (action case) or drop them (clean case), which is what this
431	/// wrapper's stderr capture did in the spawned form.
432	fn fetch_silent(repo: &Path, remote: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
433	    debug!("fetch --remote {remote} -R {}", repo.display());
434	    jj::git_fetch(repo, remote)

445	/// - **any other repo** → move `@` onto the synced `bookmark` under
446	///   the work-repo safety rules (see `reposition_work`).

449	    bookmark: &str,
450	    params: &SyncParams,
451	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
452	    if is_bot_repo(repo) {
453	        reposition_bot(repo)
454	    } else {
455	        reposition_work(repo, bookmark, params.rebase)
456	    }

468	/// Bookmark to sync for `repo`.

471	/// linear journal on `main` by design, so it pins `main` regardless
472	/// of the requested bookmark. Every other repo uses `bookmark`

478	/// Reposition the bot repo's `@` onto `main`.
479	///
480	/// The session (`.claude`) repo is a linear journal on `main`, and its
481	/// `@` normally carries live session writes:
482	///
483	/// - `@-` already the `main` tip → no-op: `@` is where it belongs,
484	///   live writes stay in the working copy. (An unconditional
485	///   `jj new main` here would churn an empty `@`'s chid/op every
486	///   sync, or strand a non-empty `@`'s live writes — and any ochid
487	///   captured against its chid — on a sibling head.)
488	/// - Errors when `@-` isn't on `main` (not an ancestor-or-equal of the
489	///   bookmark) — refuse rather than guess.
490	/// - Otherwise `main` moved: `jj new main` starts a fresh `@` on the
491	///   bookmark; the prior `@` becomes a sibling head, which is
492	///   expected for the journal. A conflict is very unlikely given
493	///   `.claude`'s content; if one ever appears the user resolves it.
494	fn reposition_bot(repo: &Path) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
495	    let parent = jj::cid_short_of(repo, "@-")?;
496	    let tip = jj::cid_short_of(repo, "main")?;
497	    if parent == tip {
498	        debug!("{}: @ already on 'main'", repo.display());
499	        return Ok(());
500	    }
501	    if !jj::matches(repo, &format!("{parent}::main"))? {
502	        return Err(format!(
503	            "{}: @- ({parent}) is not on main — refusing to reposition @",
504	            repo.display()
505	        )
506	        .into());
507	    }
508	    info!("{}: jj new main", repo.display());
509	    run(
510	        "jj",
511	        &["new", "main", "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
512	        Path::new("."),
513	    )?;
514	    Ok(())
515	}

517	/// Reposition the work repo's `@` onto the synced `bookmark`.
518	///
519	/// Let `@-` be the parent of `@`:
520	///
521	/// - `bookmark == @-` → already positioned; no-op.
522	/// - `bookmark` a proper descendant of `@-`, `@` empty →
523	///   `jj new bookmark` (jj auto-abandons the old empty `@`).
524	/// - `bookmark` a proper descendant of `@-`, `@` non-empty → rebase
525	///   `@` onto `bookmark`, but only with `rebase` set (else prompt on a
526	///   TTY; skip + inform when declined or not a TTY).
527	/// - `bookmark` not a descendant of `@-` (diverged / `@` ahead) →
528	///   leave `@` and inform why it didn't move.
529	fn reposition_work(
530	    repo: &Path,
531	    bookmark: &str,
532	    rebase: bool,
533	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
534	    let parent = jj::cid_short_of(repo, "@-")?;
535	    let tip = jj::cid_short_of(repo, bookmark)?;
536	    if tip == parent {
537	        debug!("{}: @ already on '{bookmark}'", repo.display());
538	        return Ok(());
539	    }
540	    if !jj::matches(repo, &format!("{parent}::{tip}"))? {
541	        info!(
542	            "{}: @- ({parent}) is not behind '{bookmark}' ({tip}); leaving @ in place",
543	            repo.display()
544	        );
545	        return Ok(());
546	    }
547	    // `bookmark` is a proper descendant of `@-` — safe to move a clean `@`.
548	    if at_is_empty(repo)? {
549	        info!("{}: jj new {bookmark}", repo.display());
550	        run(
551	            "jj",
552	            &["new", bookmark, "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
553	            Path::new("."),
554	        )?;
555	        return Ok(());
556	    }
557	    // `@` carries changes: rebase only on opt-in / confirmation.
558	    if !rebase && !confirm_rebase(repo)? {
559	        info!(
560	            "{}: @ has changes; left in place (pass --rebase to rebase onto '{bookmark}')",
561	            repo.display()
562	        );
563	        return Ok(());
564	    }
565	    info!("{}: rebasing @ onto '{bookmark}'", repo.display());
566	    run(
567	        "jj",
568	        &["rebase", "-b", "@", "-d", bookmark, "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
569	        Path::new("."),
570	    )?;
571	    if has_conflicts(repo)? {
572	        return Err(format!(
573	            "{}: rebase of @ onto '{bookmark}' produced conflicts",
574	            repo.display()
575	        )
576	        .into());
577	    }
578	    Ok(())
579	}

581	/// Ask whether to rebase a non-empty `@`, but only on a TTY.
582	///
583	/// Returns `Ok(false)` without prompting when stdin isn't a terminal
584	/// (scripts): the caller then skips + informs rather than blocking on
585	/// `read_line`. A `y`/`yes` (case-insensitive) answer confirms.
586	///
587	/// Under `cargo test` the harness inherits the invoking terminal's
588	/// stdin, so an in-process test reaching this path would block on
589	/// `read_line` waiting for the user — the `cfg!(test)` arm pins the
590	/// non-interactive answer instead.
591	fn confirm_rebase(repo: &Path) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
592	    if cfg!(test) || !std::io::stdin().is_terminal() {
593	        return Ok(false);
594	    }
595	    let ans = prompt(&format!(
596	        "{}: @ has changes — rebase onto the synced bookmark? [y/N] ",
597	        repo.display()
598	    ))?;
599	    Ok(matches!(ans.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str(), "y" | "yes"))
600	}

602	/// True when the working-copy commit `@` is empty (no changes).
603	fn at_is_empty(repo: &Path) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
604	    jj::matches(repo, "@ & empty()")
605	}
606	
607	/// Perform the mutation corresponding to `ctx.state` (skipped in
608	/// deprecated verify-only mode).
609	///
610	/// - `UpToDate` / `Ahead` / `NoRemote` → no-op (and no output, the state
611	///   was already logged by `log_state`).
612	/// - `Behind` → `jj bookmark set <b> -r <b>@<remote>` to fast-forward.
613	/// - `Diverged` → `jj rebase -b <b> -d <b>@<remote>`, then probe
614	///   `conflicts()`. A non-empty result means the rebase produced
615	///   conflicted commits; return `Err` so the outer revert restores the
616	///   pre-fetch state.
617	fn act_on_state(ctx: &RepoCtx, params: &SyncParams) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
618	    let repo = &ctx.path;
619	    let bookmark = repo_bookmark(repo, &params.bookmark);
620	    let remote_rev = format!("{}@{}", bookmark, params.remote);
621	    match &ctx.state {
622	        State::UpToDate | State::Ahead { .. } | State::NoRemote => Ok(()),
623	        State::Behind { .. } => {
624	            if !params.check {
625	                info!("{}: setting '{bookmark}' to {remote_rev}", repo.display());
626	                jj::bookmark_set(repo, bookmark, &remote_rev)?;
627	            }
628	            Ok(())
629	        }
630	        State::Diverged { local, remote } => {
631	            if !params.check {
632	                // `local` is either a single commit id or a comma-joined list
633	                // of heads when the bookmark is conflicted. Pick the head
634	                // that isn't the remote — that's the local-only tip. The
635	                // comma-joined path covers the jj post-fetch divergence
636	                // shape (local bookmark conflicted between old local head
637	                // and freshly-fetched remote head).
638	                let local_head = local
639	                    .split(',')
640	                    .find(|h| *h != remote)
641	                    .unwrap_or(local.as_str());
642	                info!(
643	                    "{}: rebasing {local_head} onto {remote_rev}",
644	                    repo.display()
645	                );
646	                run(
647	                    "jj",
648	                    &[
649	                        "rebase",
650	                        "-b",
651	                        local_head,
652	                        "-d",
653	                        &remote_rev,
654	                        "-R",
655	                        &repo_str(repo),
656	                    ],
657	                    Path::new("."),
658	                )?;
659	                if has_conflicts(repo)? {
660	                    return Err(format!("{}: rebase produced conflicts", repo.display()).into());
661	                }
662	            }
663	            Ok(())
664	        }
665	    }
666	}

668	/// Print a single-line summary of `state` at `info!` level.
669	fn log_state(repo: &Path, state: &State) {
670	    let r = repo.display();
671	    match state {
672	        State::UpToDate => info!("{r}: up-to-date"),
673	        State::NoRemote => info!("{r}: no remote counterpart — skipping"),
674	        State::Ahead { local, remote } => {
675	            info!("{r}: ahead (local {local} > remote {remote}); nothing to sync")
676	        }
677	        State::Behind { local, remote } => {
678	            info!("{r}: behind (local {local} < remote {remote}); fast-forward needed")
679	        }
680	        State::Diverged { local, remote } => {
681	            info!("{r}: diverged (local {local} vs remote {remote}); rebase needed")
682	        }
683	    }
684	}

686	/// Return the id of the most recent operation on `repo`.
687	///
688	/// Used as the revert target on failure. Exposed at `pub(crate)` so
689	/// `push` (0.37.0-2+) can reuse the same snapshot pattern for its
690	/// commit-stage rollback without duplicating the jj invocation.
691	pub(crate) fn current_op_id(repo: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
692	    let out = run(
693	        "jj",
694	        &[
695	            "op",
696	            "log",
697	            "--no-graph",
698	            "-n",
699	            "1",
700	            "-T",
701	            "id.short(12)",
702	            "-R",
703	            &repo_str(repo),
704	        ],
705	        Path::new("."),
706	    )?;
707	    Ok(out.trim().to_string())
708	}
709	
710	/// Restore `repo` to the operation identified by `op_id`.
711	///
712	/// Thin wrapper around `jj op restore` — drops the caller's returned
713	/// stdout. Exposed at `pub(crate)` for `push`'s commit-stage
714	/// rollback and the `revert` subcommand; sync itself no longer
715	/// auto-reverts (stop-on-error).
716	pub(crate) fn op_restore(repo: &Path, op_id: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
717	    run(
718	        "jj",
719	        &["op", "restore", op_id, "-R", &repo_str(repo)],
720	        Path::new("."),
721	    )?;
722	    Ok(())
723	}
724	
725	/// Classify the relationship between `bookmark` and `bookmark@remote`.
726	///
727	/// Uses `bookmarks(<b>)` rather than the bare name so a conflicted
728	/// bookmark (jj's representation of a diverged fetch) resolves to all
729	/// of its heads instead of erroring. When the set has multiple heads,
730	/// the bookmark is conflicted and the repo is `Diverged` by definition.
731	/// Otherwise we compare the single local head against the single
732	/// remote commit via two revset-ancestry probes.
733	///
734	/// Returns `NoRemote` when `<b>@<remote>` does not resolve — the caller
735	/// logs a skip and moves on.
736	fn classify(
737	    repo: &Path,
738	    bookmark: &str,
739	    remote: &str,
740	) -> Result<State, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
741	    let local_heads = local_bookmark_heads(repo, bookmark)?;
742	    let remote_rev = format!("{bookmark}@{remote}");
743	    let Some(remote) = try_commit_id(repo, &remote_rev)? else {
744	        return Ok(State::NoRemote);
745	    };
746	    if local_heads.is_empty() {
747	        return Err(format!("{}: bookmark '{bookmark}' does not exist", repo.display()).into());
748	    }
749	    if local_heads.len() > 1 {
750	        // Conflicted bookmark — jj's shape for post-fetch divergence.
751	        let local = local_heads.join(",");
752	        return Ok(State::Diverged { local, remote });
753	    }
754	    let local = local_heads.into_iter().next().unwrap(); // OK: `len() > 1` arm handled above, `is_empty()` handled above
755	    if local == remote {
756	        return Ok(State::UpToDate);
757	    }
758	    let local_is_anc = jj::matches(repo, &format!("{local}::{remote_rev}"))?;
759	    let remote_is_anc = jj::matches(repo, &format!("{remote_rev}::{local}"))?;
760	    Ok(match (local_is_anc, remote_is_anc) {
761	        (true, _) => State::Behind { local, remote },
762	        (false, true) => State::Ahead { local, remote },
763	        (false, false) => State::Diverged { local, remote },
764	    })
765	}
766	
767	/// Return all commit ids the `bookmark` currently points at.
768	///
769	/// Normally a one-element vector; two or more elements indicate a
770	/// conflicted bookmark (jj's representation of diverged post-fetch
771	/// state, where the local bookmark has multiple heads).
772	fn local_bookmark_heads(
773	    repo: &Path,
774	    bookmark: &str,
775	) -> Result<Vec<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
776	    jj::cids_short_of(repo, &format!("bookmarks(exact:{bookmark})"))
777	}
778	
779	/// Like `jj::cid_short_of`, but `Ok(None)` when the revset doesn't resolve.
780	///
781	/// The unresolvable-revision error (`jj::is_no_such_revision`,
782	/// typed in-process or by stderr wording when spawned) maps to
783	/// `Ok(None)` so callers can distinguish "missing" from "other
784	/// failure".
785	fn try_commit_id(repo: &Path, rev: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
786	    match jj::cid_short_of(repo, rev) {
787	        Ok(id) if id.is_empty() => Ok(None),
788	        Ok(id) => Ok(Some(id)),
789	        Err(e) if jj::is_no_such_revision(e.as_ref()) => Ok(None),
790	        Err(e) => Err(e),
791	    }
792	}
793	
794	/// Return `true` when `repo` has any conflicted commits.
795	fn has_conflicts(repo: &Path) -> Result<bool, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
796	    jj::matches(repo, "conflicts()")
797	}
798	
799	/// Convert a path to a `String` suitable for passing as a subprocess arg.
800	fn repo_str(p: &Path) -> String {
801	    p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()
802	}

1	//! `SubcommandRunner` trait
2	//!
3	//! The purpose is to simplify invoking a subcommand so `main`
4	//! can invoke any subcommand with one line:
5	//!
6	//! `Commands::Chid(args) => args.dispatch(&ctx),`
7	//!
8	//! Instead of the ~11 lines that the default `dispatch` below
9	//! now encapsulates.
10	//!
11	//! Implementors provide:
12	//!
13	//! - [`SubcommandRunner::to_params`] — build the clap-free
14	//!   `Params` from the clap `Args` (covers both `From` /
15	//!   `TryFrom` shapes uniformly via `Result<_, String>`).
16	//! - [`SubcommandRunner::run`] — the subcommand body.
17	//!
18	//! The default [`SubcommandRunner::dispatch`] builds `Params`
19	//! via `to_params`, runs via `run`, and maps the result to
20	//! `ExitCode`. Errors at any stage log via `error!` and return
21	//! `ExitCode::FAILURE`. `Context` is loaded once in `main` and
22	//! passed in by reference so a single `Context` is shared across
23	//! the (one) match arm that actually runs.
24	//!
25	//! ## See also
26	//!
27	//! - The wider CLI-args / subcommand-layer split this trait
28	//!   formalizes: [`ARCHITECTURE.md > args → Context + Params`][arch].
29	//! - Cycle design, ladder, evaluation gate:
30	//!   [`chores-10.md > 0.50.0-0`][open].
31	//! - Worked example, trait-shape decisions, naming:
32	//!   [`chores-10.md > 0.50.0-1`][port].
33	//! - First implementor: [`crate::chid`].
34	//!
35	//! [arch]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md#args--context--params
36	//! [open]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-10.md#chore-open-subcommand-trait-sweep-0500-0
37	//! [port]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/main/notes/chores/chores-10.md#refactor-subcommandrunner-trait--chid-0500-1
38	
39	use std::process::ExitCode;
40	
41	use log::error;
42	
43	use crate::context::Context;
44	
45	/// Trait implemented by every subcommand's clap `Args` type so
46	/// `main.rs` can dispatch via a single `args.dispatch(&ctx)`
47	/// call.
48	pub trait SubcommandRunner {
49	    /// The clap-free `Params` struct the subcommand body
50	    /// consumes.
51	    type Params;
52	
53	    /// Build `Params` from `Args`. `Result<_, String>` absorbs
54	    /// both `From` (return `Ok(...)`) and `TryFrom` (forward
55	    /// the error) shapes uniformly.
56	    fn to_params(&self) -> Result<Self::Params, String>;
57	
58	    /// Run the subcommand body.
59	    fn run(ctx: &Context, params: &Self::Params) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;
60	
61	    /// Default dispatch: build `Params` via `to_params`, bracket
62	    /// the run with `crate::bm_track` enter/exit, execute via
63	    /// `run`, and map the result to `ExitCode`. Errors at any
64	    /// stage log via `error!` and return `ExitCode::FAILURE`.
65	    /// `bm_track` itself emits at `debug!`, so default runs stay
66	    /// quiet — no per-call gate is needed here.
67	    fn dispatch(&self, ctx: &Context) -> ExitCode {
68	        let params = match self.to_params() {
69	            Ok(p) => p,
70	            Err(e) => {
71	                error!("{e}");
72	                return ExitCode::FAILURE;
73	            }
74	        };
75	
76	        // Command name is the first positional after the binary;
77	        // clap has already validated it by the time we reach
78	        // dispatch (top-level parse errors exit earlier).
79	        let command_name = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "?".to_string()); // OK: default when somehow invoked without a subcommand
80	
81	        crate::bm_track("enter", &command_name);
82	        let exit_code = match Self::run(ctx, &params) {
83	            Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,
84	            Err(e) => {
85	                error!("{e}");
86	                ExitCode::FAILURE
87	            }
88	        };
89	        crate::bm_track("exit ", &command_name);
90	        exit_code
91	    }
92	}

##### 0.78.0-7 refactor: context-owned repo sessions

`Context` grows the session map the `-6` review designed:
lazily-opened `RepoSession`s keyed by canonicalized repo path,
opened on first use by `Context::session` and reused for the
rest of the invocation. Has-a, never is-a: an invocation
touches 0..N repos, and a repo-less `version` never opens one.
The five verbs move from facade fns onto `RepoSession` as
methods; the facade keeps one-shot wrappers for context-less
callers.

- `SubcommandRunner::run` (and `dispatch`) take
  `&mut Context`: the sessions are exclusive mutable state,
  and the borrow checker enforcing one live session borrow at
  a time is what a `RefCell` would trade for runtime panics.
  The fifteen non-consumer subcommands change signature only.
- Verbs as `RepoSession` methods: `commit`, `describe`,
  `bookmark_set`, `git_push_bookmark`, `git_fetch`, plus the
  `one_commit` resolver and `complete_newline`.
  `DebugCallback` goes private to the session module.
- One-shot wrappers stay for the context-less callers:
  fix-desc (`describe`), init (`bookmark_set`,
  `git_push_bookmark`), repo_utils (`commit`, `describe`).
  `git_fetch`'s only caller is sync, context-ful, so its
  wrapper is deleted rather than kept unused.
- `RepoSession::snapshot` now reloads at the op-store head
  for every repo, not only colocated ones: a session outlives
  single verbs in a `Context`, and a spawned `jj` (squash,
  new, rebase, op restore) may commit operations between
  verbs. Reuse skips only the open (settings + workspace
  load); freshness is per-verb, unchanged.
- Consumers: push threads `ctx` through `mutate` and the four
  mutating stages, and its `squash-push-bot` stage passes the
  same `ctx` into squash-push, so one bot-repo session serves
  the whole run; squash-push and sync take `ctx` for their
  verb sites (`fetch_silent`, `act_on_state`). Reads stay
  one-shot facade fns.
- Tests: `test_helpers::test_ctx()` builds a
  default-user-config `Context`; the push / sync /
  squash-push integration tests pass a fresh one per op call,
  matching the production one-context-per-invocation shape.

1	//! Typed facade over jj: reads and the publish-path mutations, all
2	//! in-process through jj-lib (the jj-lib migration stage of
3	//! `notes/refactor-20260716.md`).
4	//!
5	//! Reads resolve through `common::load_repo` +
6	//! `common::resolve_revset` and `Commit` accessors; a revset that
7	//! references a working copy (`@`, `@-`, `ws@`) snapshots first
8	//! (`repo_for_read`), so "right now" questions answer about the
9	//! filesystem the way the spawned CLI's auto-snapshot did.
10	//! Mutations are `session::RepoSession` methods; the verb fns here
11	//! are one-shot wrappers (open a session, run the verb) for
12	//! context-less callers. Context-ful callers (push, squash-push,
13	//! sync) go through `Context::session`, which caches one open
14	//! session per repo for the whole invocation.
15	//!
16	//! - `matches` / `rev_exists`: does a revset match / does a
17	//!   revision resolve.
18	//! - `chid_of` / `cid_of` / `cid_short_of` / `cids_short_of`:
19	//!   change / commit ids.
20	//! - `desc_of` / `is_empty`: description and emptiness.
21	//! - `is_no_such_revision`: the typed unresolvable-revision test.
22	//! - `commit` / `describe` / `bookmark_set` / `git_push_bookmark`:
23	//!   one-shot wrappers over the session verbs. `git_fetch` has no
24	//!   wrapper: its only caller (sync) is context-ful.
25	//!
26	//! Still spawning `jj` elsewhere: `bookmark_list` /
27	//! `bookmark_list_all` here (their consumers parse the CLI listing
28	//! textually), and the call sites outside the five verbs
29	//! (`jj squash`, `jj new`, `jj rebase`, `jj op log` / `op restore`,
30	//! `jj git clone`, `jj diff --stat`, repo-init plumbing).

42	pub(crate) mod session;

44	/// Crate-standard boxed-error result, aliased locally for brevity.
45	type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;
46	
47	/// One-shot `RepoSession::commit`: update the wc commit's
48	/// description and start a new empty change on top (`jj commit`).
49	pub fn commit(repo: &Path, desc: &str) -> Result<()> {
50	    session::RepoSession::open(repo)?.commit(desc)
51	}
52	
53	/// One-shot `RepoSession::describe`: rewrite `rev`'s description
54	/// and rebase its descendants (`jj describe -r <rev> -m <desc>`).
55	pub fn describe(repo: &Path, rev: &str, desc: &str) -> Result<()> {
56	    session::RepoSession::open(repo)?.describe(rev, desc)
57	}

71	/// True when `revset` references a working copy, so the query must
72	/// snapshot before resolving (an op-store write) to see the
73	/// filesystem as it is right now, like the CLI's auto-snapshot.
74	///
75	/// A `@` is working-copy syntax (`@`, `@-`, `ws@`) unless it has
76	/// symbol characters on *both* sides, which is the remote-bookmark
77	/// form (`name@remote`).
78	fn references_working_copy(revset: &str) -> bool {
79	    let is_symbol_char =
80	        |c: char| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, '_' | '-' | '.' | '/' | '+');
81	    let chars: Vec<char> = revset.chars().collect();
82	    chars.iter().enumerate().any(|(i, &c)| {
83	        c == '@'
84	            && !(i > 0
85	                && is_symbol_char(chars[i - 1])
86	                && chars.get(i + 1).copied().is_some_and(is_symbol_char))
87	    })
88	}

90	/// Load `repo` for a read of `revset`: a working-copy-relative
91	/// revset snapshots first so "right now" questions answer about the
92	/// filesystem; anything else is a plain read-only load.
93	fn repo_for_read(
94	    repo: &Path,
95	    revset: &str,
96	) -> Result<(
97	    jj_lib::workspace::Workspace,
98	    std::sync::Arc<jj_lib::repo::ReadonlyRepo>,
99	)> {
100	    if references_working_copy(revset) {
101	        let mut ses = session::RepoSession::open(repo)?;
102	        ses.snapshot()?;
103	        Ok((ses.workspace, ses.repo))
104	    } else {
105	        common::load_repo(repo)
106	    }
107	}

109	/// Resolve `revset` in-process and return its commits, in revset
110	/// order (newest first, matching `jj log`).
111	fn commits_of(repo: &Path, revset: &str) -> Result<Vec<Commit>> {
112	    let (workspace, repo_at_head) = repo_for_read(repo, revset)?;
113	    let ids = common::resolve_revset(&workspace, &repo_at_head, revset)?;
114	    ids.iter()
115	        .map(|id| Ok(repo_at_head.store().get_commit(id)?))
116	        .collect()
117	}

119	/// True when `revset` matches at least one commit in `repo`.
120	///
121	/// A valid-but-empty revset (e.g. `conflicts()` on a clean repo)
122	/// is `Ok(false)`; an unresolvable revision is an `Err`, which
123	/// `rev_exists` folds to `false`.
124	pub fn matches(repo: &Path, revset: &str) -> Result<bool> {
125	    let (workspace, repo_at_head) = repo_for_read(repo, revset)?;
126	    Ok(!common::resolve_revset(&workspace, &repo_at_head, revset)?.is_empty())
127	}

129	/// True when `rev` resolves in `repo`.
130	///
131	/// Folds jj's unresolvable-revision error (`is_no_such_revision`,
132	/// either path) to `Ok(false)`; other failures (bad repo path,
133	/// spawn error) stay `Err`.
134	pub fn rev_exists(repo: &Path, rev: &str) -> Result<bool> {
135	    match matches(repo, rev) {
136	        Ok(found) => Ok(found),
137	        Err(e) if is_no_such_revision(e.as_ref()) => Ok(false),
138	        Err(e) => Err(e),
139	    }
140	}

143	/// `RevsetResolutionError::NoSuchRevision` (every rev query is
144	/// in-process now, so the stderr-wording fallback is gone).
145	pub fn is_no_such_revision(e: &(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)) -> bool {
146	    matches!(
147	        e.downcast_ref::<RevsetResolutionError>(),
148	        Some(RevsetResolutionError::NoSuchRevision { .. })

Rung `-7` is built and validated. Ready to commit.

**What landed** (`0.78.0-7 refactor: context-owned repo sessions`, per the design settled at the `-6` review):

- **`Context` owns the sessions** (`src/context.rs`): a private `HashMap<PathBuf, RepoSession>` keyed by canonicalized repo path, opened lazily by `Context::session(&mut self, repo)` and reused for the rest of the invocation. Has-a, never is-a; repo-less commands never open one. A `Context::new(user_config)` constructor joins `load()` so tests can build one without reading real config.
- **Verbs are `RepoSession` methods** (`src/jj/session.rs`): `commit`, `describe`, `bookmark_set`, `git_push_bookmark`, `git_fetch` moved in from `jj.rs`, along with `one_commit` and `complete_newline`; `DebugCallback` went private. One op per verb is unchanged.
- **One freshness change I want to flag**: `RepoSession::snapshot` now reloads at the op-store head for *every* repo, not only colocated ones. A cached session outlives single verbs, and spawned `jj` (squash, new, rebase, op restore) can commit operations between verbs; reloading per verb makes a reused session exactly as fresh as a per-verb open. Session reuse therefore skips only the expensive open (settings + workspace load).
- **`SubcommandRunner::run` and `dispatch` take `&mut Context`**. I chose `&mut` over `RefCell` interior mutability: the borrow checker enforces one live session borrow at a time statically, where `RefCell` would trade that for runtime panics. The fifteen non-consumer subcommands changed signature only.
- **Consumers**: push threads `ctx` through `mutate` and the four mutating stages, and `squash-push-bot` passes the same `ctx` into `squash_push`, so one bot-repo session serves the whole run; sync routes `fetch_silent` and `act_on_state` through sessions; squash-push its bookmark-set and push. Reads stay one-shot facade fns. The facade keeps one-shot verb wrappers for the context-less callers (fix-desc, init, repo_utils); `jj::git_fetch` lost its only caller and was deleted rather than kept as dead code.
- **Tests**: new `test_helpers::test_ctx()`; the push/sync/squash-push integration tests pass a fresh one per op call, matching the one-context-per-invocation production shape.
- `TODO.md`: rung marked `(done)` with a new `##### 0.78.0-7` detail section; `Cargo.toml` bumped to `0.78.0-7`.

No `unwrap`/`expect`/`unwrap_or*` sites were introduced.

**Validation**: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test` (528 tests, all green), and `cargo install --path . --locked` all passed, in that order, after the last edit.

The plain version: vc-x1 used to open a fresh jj connection for every single write it made to a repo. Now each command run opens one connection per repo the first time it needs it and keeps reusing it, while still double-checking the repo's latest state before every write, so nothing gets stale.

Ready to commit — the working-copy diff is yours to review.

Two things are going on: which symbol you hovered, and where hover docs come from at all.

**Why the hover didn't mention `Entry`.** Hover in Zed is powered by rust-analyzer, and it documents exactly the symbol under the cursor. `map_err` belongs to the `repo.canonicalize()` line — it's `Result::map_err` on the `Result<PathBuf, io::Error>` that `canonicalize` returns, and it has nothing to do with `Entry`. The `Entry::Occupied` / `Entry::Vacant` values come from the separate call three lines down, `self.sessions.entry(key)`. So the tool was giving correct information; it was just answering a narrower question than the one you had. To get the `Entry` story, hover:

- `Entry`, `into_mut`, or `insert` in the match arms — each shows its own docs (`into_mut` returning `&'a mut V` is the interesting one),
- or the binding `e` in an arm, which shows its concrete type (`OccupiedEntry` / `VacantEntry`).

If a hover ever comes up empty or thin, it's usually rust-analyzer still indexing after an edit, not a missing feature.

**Finding the real docs for `std::collections::hash_map`:**

- The canonical page is `https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/collections/hash_map/enum.Entry.html` (and `struct.HashMap.html#method.entry` on the same site).
- Offline and version-matched to your toolchain: `rustup doc std::collections::hash_map::Entry` opens that exact page from your local rustup install in a browser; bare `rustup doc --std` opens the std index.

- For non-std crates (jj-lib, clap, ...) the same docs live on docs.rs, or build them locally with `cargo doc --open`.

  The gap is accepted and recorded here, not renumbered

## Stage: stateless push

Shipped at 0.77.0
([chores](chores/chores-15.md#refactor-stateless-push)), with
[split push.rs](#stage-split-pushrs) as its first rung. Scope
grew during the cycle: preflight went too, and the resume point
was replaced by per-stage guards rather than by a derivation,
since nothing needs to decide where to begin if every stage is
safe to repeat.

Retire the push state file and derive resume from repo
reality. Prompted by the 2026-07-20 review of the split-push
extraction ("why does `Stage` live in a file?"): the file's
chief consumers are the two sanity verifiers defending
against it going stale (the 0.37.1 false-success incident is
the canonical failure).

- Standalone `squash-push` is the precedent: stateless, it
  derives everything from the repo.
- Failure-point audit (2026-07-20 session): pre-commit
  failures need no state (nothing mutated); the
  commit-window rollback is same-process; the one real
  cross-process resume (push-work failed, commits exist,
  bookmark ahead of origin, working copies clean) is
  detectable from the repos.
- Converges with the N:1 uncovered-commit detection (Todo
  "vc-x1 push: record uncovered code commits"): both need
  "committed but not yet published".

  state file, `--restart` / `--from` / `--status`, the
  stale-state verifier, the `[push]` state config keys and
  the `.gitignore` coherence check are gone, and so is
  preflight, whose `sync --check` self-spawn was what forced
  the tests' stage-skipping flag. What replaced the resume

  each stage no-ops when its work is done, so a rerun is a
  run. The in-process `jj op` rollback stays.

  file. Moot for the trapezoid stage anyway, now that it is

  [trapezoid recipe](cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe):
  its step 4 becomes a bare `vc-x1 push <bookmark>`, because
  the post-reshape repos are exactly the state
  reality-derived resume recognizes. Docs rider on the rung
  that deletes the flag.

## Stage: jj-lib migration

Migrate the facade internals to jj-lib (already a dependency
for read-only commands); removes jj and git spawning
entirely.

- Reads first: `jj log` templates become `Commit` accessors
  (the `src/jj.rs` facade internals; `common::load_repo` /
  `resolve_revset` are the existing in-process machinery).

  working-copy auto-snapshot, since push asks "uncommitted
  changes *right now*?", so the in-process form must
  snapshot first, and a snapshot is an op-store write:
  those reads move with the mutation lift, not before.
- Then mutations: commit, describe, bookmark set/track,
  fetch, push, which is the workspace/transaction/op-store
  lift.

  retry) with real error types, the fix vehicle for the
  bugs.md `bookmark-set` lock race [[1]].

  (jj-lib already pulls gix in).

# Bugs

Known defects we're aware of but haven't scheduled a fix for.
Each entry describes what goes wrong, when, and the cost of
the failure. Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` …) the same way
as `## Todo` in `TODO.md`; run
`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber after
insert / delete / reorder.

## Bugs

1. **`push` `bookmark-set` races the git index lock.**
   `jj bookmark set` on the colocated work repo failed twice
   (the 0.69.0-3 and 0.69.0-4 pushes, same stage) with
   "Failed to reset Git HEAD state … could not acquire lock
   for `.git/index` … after 1 attempt(s)"; the lockfile was
   already gone on inspection seconds later. Seen again at
   the 0.75.0-2 push (which also triggered #3) and the
   0.77.0-0 push (2026-07-28) — four occurrences, always at
   `bookmark-set`, always transient.
   - **Cost:** push aborts mid-flow (rollback restored both
     repos cleanly both times); recovery is a `--restart`
     rerun, which succeeded both times.
   - The bot thinks a git-aware watcher (shell prompt,
     editor) briefly re-reads the repo after the commit
     stages touch `.git`, holding the index lock exactly
     when `bookmark-set` resets git HEAD; jj gives up after
     a single attempt.
   - **Fix direction** (two options, possibly combined):
     - retry with short backoff around the bookmark-set
       stage (or all jj invocations that reset git HEAD
       state)
     - use jj-lib in-process instead of spawning `jj`
       commands (suggested 2026-07-15) — the lock
       contention is external, so this alone doesn't
       remove the race, but the retry loop becomes ours
       (catch the lock error, back off, retry) with real
       error types instead of stderr parsing; this is the
       refactor program's
       [jj-lib migration stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-jj-lib-migration)

2. **stdout output panics on a closed pipe (EPIPE).**
   `vc-x1 bot-session <file> | head` panics once `head`
   closes the pipe: the logger's `println!` aborts with
   "failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe". Repo-wide
   behavior of the `info!` → `println!` path, but
   bot-session (0.70.0-2) is the first subcommand whose
   output routinely feeds a pager/filter. Found during
   0.70.0-2 verification.
   - **Cost:** ugly panic + backtrace hint instead of the
     Unix-conventional silent exit; output before the pipe
     closed is intact.
   - **Fix direction:** handle EPIPE in the logger (write
     via `writeln!` to a locked stdout and exit 0 on
     `BrokenPipe`), or reset SIGPIPE to default on unix at
     startup.

3. **`push` resume-after-rollback replays from the wrong
   stage.** Observed at the 0.75.0-2 push (2026-07-23): the
   `push` `bookmark-set` git-index-lock race fired, the error path
   `op restore`d both repos — undoing `commit-work` /
   `commit-bot` — but the state file still said
   `stage = bookmark-set`. The rerun resumed there,
   *skipping the commit stages*: bookmark-set pinned the
   bookmarks to `@-` (the **previous** cycle commit),
   push-work no-op re-pushed it, and squash-push-bot
   squashed the accumulated session data into the
   already-published previous bot commit and republished
   it. The completion sanity check caught the chid
   mismatch and warned, but after the damage.
   - **Cost:** no data loss (work `@` kept the uncommitted
     changes; the bot chid is rebase-stable so the ochid
     pairing survived) — but session data landed under the
     previous commit's title, and the published bot commit
     was rewritten in place.

     about where the run stopped: rollback rewinds the
     *repos* to pre-commit, but not the *state* to the
     `message` stage. Any `Err` between `commit-work` and
     the stage save has the same shape.

     state file in the same breath — or retire the state
     file entirely and derive resume from repo reality,

##### 0.78.0-8 fix: jj-lib index-lock retry

The bugs.md #1 fix, landing on the `-7` frame as ordered: gix
gives `.git/index.lock` a single attempt, and a git-aware
watcher can hold it exactly when a mutation resets the index,
so the session retries the colocated git half itself. Plus the
planned rider: init's `git init --bare` becomes a gix call,
the last `git` spawn in init.

  (`finish_tx`'s HEAD/index reset + ref export, the snapshot's
  intent-to-add + ref export), both strictly before the
  transaction commit, so a retried closure never doubles an
  op-store write.

The timeline is the other way around — the lock is planted by the *main* thread before `bookmark_set` ever runs; the spawned thread only *removes* it. Walking through it:

1. **`std::fs::write(&lock, "")`** — this runs on the main thread, synchronously, before anything else. From this instant, `.git/index.lock` exists, simulating some other process holding the lock. This is the "plant".
2. **`thread::spawn(...)`** — the thread starts, but its first action is to sleep 120 ms. It does not create or acquire anything; its only job is `remove_file` — the *release* — 120 ms later.
3. **`bookmark_set(...)`** — called while the lock file is already sitting there. When `finish_tx` reaches the index write, gix tries to create `.git/index.lock`, finds it exists, and fails immediately (one attempt, no waiting — that's the whole bug). The retry loop classifies it as contention and backs off: 25 ms, 50 ms, 100 ms...
4. At ~120 ms, the thread deletes the file. The retry's next attempt (attempt 3 or 4, somewhere in the 75–175 ms window) acquires the lock cleanly and the mutation completes.

So `bookmark_set` cannot "use the lock and release it before the thread" — it can't acquire the lock at all while the planted file exists, and the file exists from step 1 with no gap. The only ordering the test depends on is that the release (120 ms) lands inside the retry budget (~375 ms), which has a comfortable margin.

Your suggested shape — waiting before `bookmark_set` — would actually break the test: if the lock were released before `bookmark_set` starts, the first attempt would succeed and the retry path would never execute. The test would pass against code with no retry at all. The point of the current shape is that attempt 1 *must* fail (lock present from t=0) and only a later attempt can succeed, so the test genuinely fails on the pre-fix code.

The plain version: the file blocking git is put in place before the operation starts, and the background thread's sleep is just a timer for taking it away mid-operation — so the operation is guaranteed to trip over it first and recover only because it retries.

content.text:
You've got the sequence right now, and just one refinement to the model: there is no lock *object* being held by anyone in this test — the file's existence **is** the lock. That's git's lockfile protocol:

- "Acquiring the index lock" means *creating* `.git/index.lock` with create-new semantics (fail if it already exists). Whoever succeeds at creating it holds the lock.
- "Releasing" means *deleting* (or renaming) that file. Nothing is held open in between; a process could crash and the stale file would still "hold" the lock — that's why gix's error message mentions the lockfile "might need manual deletion".

So in the test:

- `fs::write` creates a plain empty file and returns immediately — it holds nothing afterward. But by the protocol, the lock now reads as "held by someone" to any git/gix code that comes along.
- `bookmark_set` on the main thread reaches the index write; gix tries to create `index.lock`, sees it already exists, and errors on its single attempt. Our retry loop catches that and sleeps (25, 50, 100 ms...) — so yes, the main thread spends this whole stretch inside `bookmark_set`, but it's failing-and-sleeping, not blocked waiting on any lock primitive.
- The spawned thread wakes at 120 ms and calls `remove_file` — an ordinary unlink, no lock involved on its side either. The protocol now reads "lock free".
- `bookmark_set`'s next retry successfully creates `index.lock` itself, writes the index, removes its own lockfile, and returns. Then `join`, then the assert.

Your only remaining adjustment: `write` never "used and released" anything, and `remove_file` doesn't "use the lock" — both are ordinary file operations that happen to manipulate the file whose existence git treats as the lock.

The plain version: git's lock is just a file with a special name. Making the file claims the lock; deleting it gives the lock up. The test fakes a lock-holder by creating that file directly, and fakes the holder letting go by deleting it — no actual locking machinery runs except inside gix when it finally gets to create the file itself.

For future reference, the recipe is:

The plain version: tests don't print debug messages because nothing in a test run is listening for them; you temporarily plug in the same listener the real CLI uses with `-v`, tell the test runner not to hide the output, and take the plug back out afterwards.
