Two separate things went wrong there, and one of them is just a typo:

1. **The test-name filter matched nothing**: you ran `mature_survives_transient_index_lock`, but the test is `mutation_survives_transient_index_lock` — hence `running 0 tests ... 485 filtered out`. Any substring works, so `survives_transient` is enough.

2. **`CliLogger::new(...)` builds a logger but installs nothing.** It returns a `CliLogger` value that you immediately drop — it never calls `log::set_boxed_logger` (registering it as the global sink) or `log::set_max_level` (without which `debug!` is compiled to a cheap early-out). `init` is the function that does both; its signature is `init(verbose: u8, log_path: Option<&str>)`, so the call is `CliLogger::init(1, None)` — plain `1`, not a `LevelFilter` (my guess is you passed `Some(LevelFilter::Debug)` into `init`, which is `new`'s signature, and that's the compile error you hit). Also: `RUST_LOG` and `SWC_DEBUG` do nothing here — this logger never reads env vars; that's an `env_logger` convention.

30	This is experiment 1 to explore creating a Vibe Coding (vc) environment.
31	We will investigate ways of using the dual jj-git repo concept, explored
32	in [hw-jjg-bot](https://github.com/winksaville/hw-jjg-bot.git) to
33	initially make it easy to see how the code base evolved. This is
34	made possible by the fact that we have two repos one with the code
35	and one with the conversation with the bot.
36	
37	I've chosen the jj-git environment because jj provides the concept that
38	each commit has an immutable changeID as well as the mutable commitID
39	of git. The idea is that each commit made on repo A writes the
40	changeID in the commit message to repo B. Thus there is a cross reference
41	between the two repos and this will allow vc-x1 to show how the repo
42	evolved and the entity (bot or human) can more clearly understand **how** and
43	most importantly **why** the code evolved.
44	
45	The solution space is wide open, from trivial CLI, web or app based
46	(mobile/non-mobile). In addition, I could see this as an extension to
47	existing programming editors like vscode and zed or even creating our
48	own IDE for vc.
49	
50	See [Initial commit with dual jj-git repos](./notes/chores/chores-01.md#initial-commit-with-dual-jj-git-repos)
51	for how the initial commit was created with the dual jj-git repos. After
52	doing so and I then created this README.md file.
53	
54	## Terminology
55	
56	A vc-x1 workspace pairs two jj-git repos, and this README names
57	their two sides **work** and **bot**:
58	
59	- **work repo**: the repo at the project root, holding the work
60	  product itself (source code, docs, the repo you would have
61	  anyway).
62	- **bot repo**: the `.claude` repo nested inside it, holding the
63	  bot's session data (the conversation that produced the work).
64	- **work** / **bot**: the two sides as roles, used wherever a
65	  command or doc needs to say which repo it means (e.g. push's
66	  `commit-work` / `commit-bot` stages).
67	
68	A few naming conventions this project keeps, to avoid ambiguous
69	jargon:
70	
71	- **path** is reserved for a filesystem location, qualified as
72	  **relative** or **absolute** when it matters (e.g. `../other`,
73	  `/home/you/repo`).
74	- a configuration setting is a **config key**, e.g.
75	  `bot-session.col-width` (its TOML table and key joined by `.`);
76	  not a "path".
77	- a datum in a transcript's `--fields` inventory is a **field**,
78	  e.g. `message.content[].type`, its levels joined by `.`, with
79	  `[]` marking array elements.
80	
81	## Usage
82	
83	```
84	vc-x1 list [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # List commits in a jj repo
85	vc-x1 desc [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # Show full description of a commit
86	vc-x1 chid [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # Print changeID(s) for a revision
87	vc-x1 show [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # Show commit details and diff summary
88	vc-x1 bot-session <FILE> [OPTS]        # Display a session transcript as a conversation
89	vc-x1 validate-desc [OPTS]                 # Validate commit descriptions
90	vc-x1 fix-desc [OPTS]                     # Fix commit descriptions (dry-run default)
91	vc-x1 validate-todo [FILE]                # Check todo-file entry numbering
92	vc-x1 fix-todo [FILE]                     # Renumber todo file (dry-run default)
93	vc-x1 validate-bot [OPTS]                 # Check the bot repo is published
94	vc-x1 config [OPTS]                       # Print / validate settable config keys
95	vc-x1 clone <REPO> [NAME] [OPTS]          # Clone a dual-repo project
96	vc-x1 init <TARGET> [OPTS]                # Create a new dual-repo project
97	vc-x1 symlink [TARGET] [OPTS]             # Create Claude Code project symlink
98	vc-x1 sync [OPTS]                          # Fetch + sync both repos to their remotes
99	vc-x1 revert [OPTS]                        # Restore repos to a prior operation
100	vc-x1 squash-push [BOOKMARK] [OPTS]        # Squash @ into @-, advance a bookmark, push
101	vc-x1 push [BOOKMARK] [OPTS]               # Commit both repos, push work, squash-push bot
102	vc-x1 --version                            # Print version
103	vc-x1 --help                           # Print help
104	```
105	
106	**The `..` notation:** dots on the revision show which direction to
107	list commits:
108	
109	- `x..`: x at top, ancestors below (older commits)
110	- `..x`: descendants above (newer commits), x at bottom
111	- `..x..`: both directions, x in the middle
112	
113	COMMITS is the total number of commits to show (x is always included).
114	Without dots, `x` with a count defaults to `x..` (ancestors).
115	For `..x..`, the budget is split: ancestors get the extra on odd counts.
116	
117	```
118	vc-x1 list -r @              # just @ (1 commit)
119	vc-x1 list -r @.. -n 5       # @ + 4 ancestors (5 commits, @ at top)
120	vc-x1 list -r ..@ -n 3       # 2 descendants + @ (3 commits, @ at bottom)
121	vc-x1 list -r ..@.. -n 3     # 1 descendant, @, 1 ancestor (3 commits)
122	vc-x1 list -r ..@.. -n 4     # 1 descendant, @, 2 ancestors (4 commits)
123	```
124	
125	### Shell completion
126	
127	vc-x1 provides tab completion for all subcommands and flags using claps
128	[unstable-dynamic](https://docs.rs/clap_complete/latest/clap_complete/env/struct.CompleteEnv.html)
129	only feature. It is a "simple" implementation and does not handle completing
130	revisions but still useful. To enable it, add one of the following to your shell's startup file:
131	
132	```bash
133	# bash (~/.bashrc)
134	source <(COMPLETE=bash vc-x1)
135	
136	# zsh (~/.zshrc)
137	source <(COMPLETE=zsh vc-x1)
138	
139	# fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish)
140	source (COMPLETE=fish vc-x1 | psub)
141	```
142	
143	Completions are generated dynamically by the binary, so they stay in
144	sync with the installed version automatically.
145	
146	### Positional shorthand
147	
148	REVISION and COMMITS can be given as positional arguments, omitting
149	`-r` and `-n`:
150	
151	```
152	vc-x1 list x                # just x (1 commit)
153	vc-x1 list x 5              # x.. 5 -> x + 4 ancestors (5 commits)
154	vc-x1 list x.. 5            # same as above
155	vc-x1 list ..x 3            # 2 descendants + x (3 commits)
156	vc-x1 list ..x.. 3          # 1 descendant, x, 1 ancestor (3 commits)
157	vc-x1 list ..x.. 1          # just x (1 commit)
158	```
159	
160	**Defaults:** with no arguments, REVISION is `@` and COMMITS is 1
161	(just the working copy).
162	
163	Named flags `-r`/`--revision`, `-n`/`--commits`, `-R`/`--repo`, and
164	`-s`/`--scope` take precedence over positional arguments.
165	
166	### Multi-repo queries
167	
168	`-s`/`--scope` selects workspace sides by role keyword; `work` is the
169	work repo, `bot` is the `.claude` repo, `work,bot` is both. The
170	workspace root is found by walking up from cwd (the existing
171	`find_workspace_root` rule).
172	
173	```
174	vc-x1 chid -s work,bot          # both sides of the workspace
175	vc-x1 chid -s work              # just the work repo
176	vc-x1 chid -s bot               # just the bot repo
177	vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot    # works with chid / desc / list / show
178	```
179	
180	`-R`/`--repo` takes a single path. Used alone it points at one jj
181	repo (workspace lookup is skipped); combined with `-s` it overrides
182	the workspace root for the role lookup:
183	
184	```
185	vc-x1 chid -R .                  # single repo at .
186	vc-x1 chid -R .claude            # single repo at .claude
187	vc-x1 chid -R ../other -s work,bot   # both sides of ../other workspace
188	```
189	
190	Defaults preserve prior behavior: no flag -> `[.]`, `-R foo` alone
191	-> `[foo]`. When multiple repos are resolved (any `-s` that names
192	more than one role), output is labeled with bold `=== path ===`
193	headers by default. Control the label with `-l`/`--label` and
194	`-L`/`--no-label`:
195	
196	```
197	vc-x1 chid -s work,bot            # default label: === path ===
198	vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -l "---"   # custom label:  --- path ---
199	vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L         # no label (raw output)
200	```
201	
202	Examples:
203	
204	```
205	$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot
206	=== . ===
207	kwoyvposvsmv
208	
209	=== .claude ===
210	zzpksklxyrnw
211	
212	$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L
213	kwoyvposvsmv
214	zzpksklxyrnw
215	
216	$ vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot
217	=== . ===
218	kwoyvposvsmv eae175c3c1b5 (no description set)
219	pqxtxxpnsmot b0c46930a640 Reorganize notes (0.19.1)
220	ssokyszzwsxw eeb15bc6d839 Unify .. notation and CLI (0.19.0)
221	
222	=== .claude ===
223	zzpksklxyrnw 2388185e42ee (no description set)
224	tzupykyyvnrp 81ce22e34d41 Reorganize notes (0.19.1)
225	slmkmroqtqtp 1c33ccaa567d Unify .. notation and CLI (0.19.0)
226	
227	$ vc-x1 desc -r @- -s work,bot
228	=== . ===
229	pqxtxxpnsmot b0c46930a640 Reorganize notes: move older done items to done.md, update todos (0.19.1)
230	
231	    Move completed items [1]-[13] and their references from todo.md to done.md.
232	    Replace completed jj-organization todo with new items.
233	
234	    ochid: tzupykyyvnrp
235	
236	=== .claude ===
237	tzupykyyvnrp 81ce22e34d41 Reorganize notes: move older done items to done.md, update todos (0.19.1)
238	
239	    Session: reviewed and committed notes reorganization for 0.19.1.
240	
241	    ochid: pqxtxxpnsmot
242	
243	$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -l "---"
244	--- . ---
245	kwoyvposvsmv
246	
247	--- .claude ---
248	zzpksklxyrnw
249	```
250	
251	Most decoration strings work unquoted (`---`, `===`, `>>>`, `:::`,
252	`+++`). Use single quotes for strings containing shell metacharacters
253	like `*`, `!`, `#`, `$`, or `~` (e.g. `-l '***'`). Double quotes
254	won't protect against `!` (bash history expansion).
255	
256	With a single repo resolved, no label is printed, backward
257	compatible with the no-flag default. Multi-repo (`-s work,bot`) is
258	supported for `chid`, `desc`, `list`, and `show`. `squash-push`
259	remains single-repo.
260	
261	`-s` is keyword-only: `work`, `bot`, `work,bot`, `bot,work`.
262	Path-based single-repo operation uses `-R` (above).

264	### bot-session
265	
266	Display a Claude Code session transcript
267	(`.claude/<uuid>.jsonl`) as a readable conversation. The
268	transcript format is undocumented and evolves; parsing is
269	tolerant: unknown entry types are skipped and counted,
270	malformed lines (e.g. a live session's truncated last line)
271	warn to stderr and never fail the run.
272	
273	For what the transcript format looks like (entries, entry
274	types, the `.`/`[]` field notation) and an example that walks
275	a small sample through these commands, see
276	[notes/transcript-format.md](notes/transcript-format.md).
277	
278	Output is composed of eight **items**, each independently
279	toggleable:
280	
281	| Item | Emits | Default |
282	|------|-------|---------|
283	| `summary` | trailing stats line (shown / hidden / skipped counts) | on |
284	| `headers` | `=== role 2026-07-17 04:17:09Z ===` turn headers (UTC) | on |
285	| `user` | typed user prompts | on |
286	| `assistant` | assistant reply text | on |
287	| `tool` | `[tool] Name: gist` call one-liners | on |
288	| `thinking` | `[thinking]` blocks | off |
289	| `results` | `[result]` / `[result:error]` lines (capped by `--result-lines`) | off |
290	| `meta` | meta user lines, `--- system ... ---` lines, sidechain entries | off |
291	
292	Toggle with `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` (last one wins).
293	`--all` / `--none` reset the base (every item on / off) and then
294	per-item flags adjust (`--no-all` and `--no-none` are aliases
295	of `--none` and `--all`). Bookkeeping line types
296	(file-history snapshots, progress markers, ...) are never
297	rendered; they're counted in the summary as "skipped".
298	
299	Default items resolve git-style, most specific wins:
300	
301	1. CLI `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags
302	2. workspace `.vc-config.toml`: `[bot-session].items`
303	3. user `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`: `[bot-session].items`
304	4. built-in: `headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`
305	
306	```toml
307	# In ~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml (all your workspaces) or
308	# <workspace>/.vc-config.toml (this workspace, committed):
309	[bot-session]
310	items = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
311	```
312	
313	```
314	# Default conversation view
315	vc-x1 bot-session .claude/<uuid>.jsonl
316	
317	# Everything: thinking, tool results, meta/system too
318	vc-x1 bot-session --all FILE
319	
320	# Prompts only: what was asked, nothing else
321	vc-x1 bot-session --none --user FILE
322	
323	# Default view minus tool calls and headers
324	vc-x1 bot-session --no-tool --no-headers FILE
325	
326	# Slices by source JSONL line (same unit in every view)
327	vc-x1 bot-session --lines 40 FILE      # first 40 source lines
328	vc-x1 bot-session --lines -15 FILE     # last 15 source lines
329	vc-x1 bot-session --lines 100,20 FILE  # 20 lines from Index 100
330	vc-x1 bot-session --lines 100,-20 FILE # 20 lines ending at Index 100
331	vc-x1 bot-session --lines 0 FILE       # stats summary only
332	```
333	
334	| Flag | Description |
335	|------|-------------|
336	| `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` | Add / remove one of the eight items (last one wins) |
337	| `--all` / `--none` | Base: every item on / off (aliases `--no-none` / `--no-all`) |
338	| `--lines SPEC` | Slice by source JSONL line, 0-based Index (`N` first, `-N` last, `I,C` from I, `I,-C` ending at I; `0` = summary only); the same unit in every view |
339	| `--result-lines N` | Max lines shown per tool result [default: 10]; `0` = unlimited. Resolves CLI > workspace `.vc-config.toml` `[bot-session].result-lines` > user config > built-in, same as `[bot-session].items` |
340	
341	Cut points show an `... (N source lines skipped)` marker, and a
342	sliced run's summary ends with `--lines selected K of M source
343	lines`; its stats describe only the slice. Timestamps are shown as UTC
344	(`Z`) exactly when the source timestamp carries it, observed
345	always, but the format is undocumented, so anything else would
346	pass through verbatim.
347	
348	**Alternate views.** The transcript format is undocumented
349	and evolves, so bot-session doubles as a schema explorer. The
350	parser keeps every field Anthropic writes while the typed
351	layer consumes a known subset; the difference is the
352	unexplored surface:
353	
354	| Flag | View |
355	|------|------|
356	| `--fields` | Field inventory, grouped by each line's `type`: every field observed (e.g. `message.content[].type`, with `.` for nesting and `[]` for array elements) with its count, value kinds, and short samples |
357	| `--unknown` | Like `--fields`, but only fields the typed layer does not consume: the unmodeled / new surface |
358	| `--raw` | Pretty-printed source lines (unparseable lines pass through verbatim); no summary or markers |
359	| `--per-line` | With `--fields`/`--unknown` (implies `--fields`): one fields section per source line instead of aggregating |
360	| `--col-width N` | First column width in these views [default: 68]; longer field names overflow. Resolves CLI > workspace `.vc-config.toml` `[bot-session].col-width` > user config > built-in, same as `[bot-session].items` |
361	
362	The default 68 aligns the type column for ~99% of observed field
363	names; only a tail of `snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute
364	path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be arbitrarily
365	long, overflow.
366	
367	`--lines` uses the same source-line unit here, e.g.
368	`--fields --lines 0,1` inventories just the first line.
369	`--fields`/`--unknown` ignore item flags; `--raw` conflicts
370	with them.
371	
372	```
373	# What does this format actually contain today?
374	vc-x1 bot-session --fields FILE
375	
376	# What don't we model yet / what did Anthropic add?
377	vc-x1 bot-session --unknown FILE
378	
379	# Inspect one entry in full (source line 42)
380	vc-x1 bot-session --raw --lines 42,1 FILE
381	
382	# Walk a region line by line, fields-table style
383	vc-x1 bot-session --per-line --lines 40,5 FILE
384	```

386	### validate-desc
387	
388	Read-only scan of commit descriptions against the other repo. The other
389	repo is read from `.vc-config.toml` (`repos.bot`) by default,
390	or overridden with `--other-repo`. Reports status per commit: `ok`
391	(valid ochid), `lost` (ochid: lost), `none` (ochid: none), `err`
392	(issues found), or `miss` (no ochid trailer).
393	
394	```
395	# Validate all ancestors of @ (reads other repo from .vc-config.toml)
396	vc-x1 validate-desc @..
397	
398	# Validate with explicit other repo
399	vc-x1 validate-desc --other-repo .claude @..
400	
401	# Validate specific range
402	vc-x1 validate-desc -r @.. -n 20
403	```
404	
405	Use `--help` for the full status label legend.
406	
407	### fix-desc
408	
409	Fix commit descriptions against the other repo. Default is dry-run;
410	use `--no-dry-run` to write changes. Reads other repo from
411	`.vc-config.toml` by default.
412	
413	```
414	# Dry-run: show what would be fixed
415	vc-x1 fix-desc @..
416	
417	# Actually fix
418	vc-x1 fix-desc @.. --no-dry-run
419	
420	# Add missing ochid trailers by matching title
421	vc-x1 fix-desc @.. --add-missing
422	
423	# Limit fixes
424	vc-x1 fix-desc @.. --no-dry-run -m 3
425	
426	# Use a fallback for IDs not found in other repo
427	vc-x1 fix-desc @.. --fallback /.claude/lost
428	```
429	
430	| Flag | Description |
431	|------|-------------|
432	| `--other-repo <PATH>` | Override other repo from .vc-config.toml |
433	| `--no-dry-run` | Write fixes [default: dry-run] |
434	| `--add-missing` | Infer and add ochid for commits without one |
435	| `-m, --max-fixes <N>` | Stop fixing after N commits changed [default: all] |
436	| `--fallback <VALUE>` | Replacement for IDs not found in other repo |
437	| `--id-len <N>` | Expected changeID length [default: 12] |
438	| `--title <TEXT>` | Replace commit title at the same time |
439	
440	Use `--help` for the full status label legend.

442	### validate-todo
443	
444	Check that the `## Todo` and `## Bugs` sections of a todo file
445	are numbered `1..N` in document order, with continuation-line
446	indent matching each entry's number-prefix width. Read-only;
447	exits non-zero if any entry needs fixing.
448	
449	```
450	# Check TODO.md (the default)
451	vc-x1 validate-todo
452	
453	# Check a specific file
454	vc-x1 validate-todo path/to/todo.md
455	```
456	
457	Each flagged entry prints its corrected first line and a
458	`[line: ...]` tag: the entry's line number and what is off
459	(`was N`, `indent A -> B`). Use `fix-todo` to apply the fixes.
460	
461	### fix-todo
462	
463	Renumber a todo file's `## Todo` and `## Bugs` sections to
464	`1..N` and normalize each entry's continuation-line indent.
465	Dry-run by default, printing each changed entry's corrected
466	line so the output is the result; `--no-dry-run` writes the
467	file in place.
468	
469	```
470	# Dry-run: print the corrected lines
471	vc-x1 fix-todo
472	
473	# Renumber the file in place
474	vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run
475	
476	# Operate on a specific file
477	vc-x1 fix-todo path/to/todo.md
478	```
479	
480	| Flag | Description |
481	|------|-------------|
482	| `--no-dry-run` | Write the renumbered file in place [default: dry-run] |
483	
484	### validate-bot
485	
486	Check the bot repo is in its expected at-rest state: `main`
487	matching `main@origin`, with its remote refs tracked. At rest the
488	two always match, because the bookmark only moves inside a `push` /
489	`squash-push` run, which publishes it in the same invocation, so
490	a mismatch means an earlier publish was lost. Read-only and cheap
491	(two `jj` lookups, no build steps); exits non-zero on any finding
492	and fixes nothing. Resolve with `vc-x1 squash-push -R <bot-repo>`.
493	
494	```
495	# Check ./.claude (run from the project root)
496	vc-x1 validate-bot
497	
498	# Explicit bot-repo path
499	vc-x1 validate-bot -R path/to/.claude
500	```
501	
502	| Flag | Description |
503	|------|-------------|
504	| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Path to the bot repo [default: .claude] |
505	
506	`vc-x1 squash-push` reports the condition and proceeds, since
507	publishing is its job. `vc-x1 push` no longer checks it: a bot
508	repo that hasn't been squash-pushed yet isn't a broken state, and
509	the next push publishes it anyway.

511	### config
512	
513	Print the settable config keys for a target config file as an
514	annotated, commented schema: for each key its description, the
515	command/context it's `used by`, its default (or a value marked
516	`# example` when there is no default), and a commented
517	assignment line ready to paste in. The schema is generated from
518	one in-code registry, so it can't drift from what the code
519	actually reads.
520	
521	- `[TARGET]`: `work`, `bot`, `work,bot` (default), or an
522	  explicit config-file path. The keywords resolve against the
523	  surrounding workspace's `.vc-config.toml` files and filter to
524	  that side's keys; a path carries no side information, so it
525	  gets the whole schema. The user config
526	  (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`) has no keyword and is reached
527	  only by passing its path.
528	- `--validate`: instead of printing, load the target's actual
529	  config file(s) and flag any key the schema doesn't recognize
530	  (a typo, a key in the wrong section, or an unknown key), plus,
531	  for keyword targets, the legacy-schema rejection and the
532	  resolved-agreement invariant of a dual workspace's `[repos]`
533	  registries. Exits non-zero if any problem is found. This is an
534	  opt-in strict check; a normal config load silently ignores
535	  unknown keys, for forward-compatibility.
536	
537	A short sample of the printed schema (workspace home):
538	
539	```
540	[bot-session]

712	### sync
713	
714	Fetch and sync a set of repos to their remotes in one atomic
715	operation: fetch, converge the bookmark, reposition `@`. Repo set
716	defaults to the dual-repo workspace pair (`.` and `.claude`);
717	narrow it with `-s` / `--scope`, or point at a different workspace
718	root or single repo with `-R` / `--repo`. There are no modes:
719	verify-then-act happens inside a single invocation against one
720	fetch snapshot (a separate check-then-apply pair of runs would
721	race the remote).
722	
723	Per repo, `sync` classifies the local bookmark against its remote:
724	
725	| State | Meaning | Action |
726	|------|---------|--------|
727	| up-to-date | local == remote | none |
728	| behind | local is ancestor of remote | `jj bookmark set <b> -r <b>@<remote>` |
729	| ahead | remote is ancestor of local | none (push is a separate step) |
730	| diverged | neither is ancestor | `jj rebase -b <local-head> -d <b>@<remote>` |
731	| no remote | bookmark has no `@<remote>` counterpart | none, skip |
732	
733	`--bookmark` names a **work-repo** bookmark only: the bot repo
734	is a linear journal on `main` by design, so its side of every step
735	(tracking preflight, classify, act, reposition) always uses `main`
736	regardless of the flag.
737	
738	After the bookmark action above, `sync` repositions `@` onto the
739	freshly-synced bookmark as a final pass, run after every repo syncs
740	cleanly. The rule differs by repo (`@-` is the parent of `@`; `<b>`
741	is the synced `--bookmark`):
742	
743	- **Work repo** (the workspace root):
744	  - `@` is clean (empty) and `<b>` sits ahead of `@-` on the same
745	    line -> `jj new <b>` starts a fresh `@` on the new tip (the old
746	    empty `@` is auto-abandoned).
747	  - `@` has changes -> `sync` asks before moving it; pass `--rebase`
748	    to answer yes up front (`jj rebase -b @ -d <b>`). Declining, or
749	    not being a TTY with no `--rebase`, leaves `@` in place and says
750	    so.
751	  - `@` already sits on `<b>`, or `<b>` isn't on `@-`'s line
752	    (diverged / `@` ahead) -> `@` is left untouched, with a note why.
753	- **Bot repo** (`.claude`): no-op when `@-` is already the
754	  `main` tip, so `@` keeps its change id and any live session writes
755	  stay in the working copy. When `main` moved, `jj new main` starts
756	  a fresh empty `@` on the new tip; the prior `@` (e.g. `/exit`'s
757	  trailing session writes) is preserved as a sibling head. If `@-`
758	  isn't on `main`, `sync` errors rather than strand it.
759	
760	On any failure during fetch/classify/act/reposition (conflicted
761	rebase, subprocess error, anything) `sync` **stops where the
762	failing step stopped**. Nothing is auto-reverted, so the state can
763	be inspected as-is (jj's operation log holds everything; nothing is
764	lost by stopping). Before acting, sync persists each repo's
765	pre-sync `jj op` id to `<repo>/.vc-x1/sync-state.toml`; the failure
766	report lists every repo's op id and the undo is explicit:
767	`vc-x1 revert` (see [revert](#revert)), or per repo
768	`jj op restore <op> -R <repo>`. On full success the snapshots are
769	cleared, since a stale file must not become a revert target later.
770	
771	```
772	vc-x1 sync                            # workspace-default scope
773	vc-x1 sync --rebase                   # rebase a dirty @ onto the bookmark without asking
774	vc-x1 sync --scope=work               # only the work repo
775	vc-x1 sync --scope=bot                # only the bot repo
776	vc-x1 sync --scope=work,bot           # both (explicit form of the dual default)
777	vc-x1 sync -R ../other                # sync ../other as a single repo
778	vc-x1 sync -R ../other --scope=work,bot   # ../other as workspace root
779	```
780	
781	**Repo set resolution.** `-R` and `--scope` compose:
782	
783	1. Neither: workspace-default scope, `work,bot` if
784	   `repos.bot` is non-empty, else `work`. POR (no
785	   `.vc-config.toml`) -> `work` resolved to cwd.
786	2. `-R PATH` alone: sync just the repo at `PATH`.
787	3. `--scope=work|bot|work,bot` alone: workspace roles, resolved
788	   via the discovered workspace root's `.vc-config.toml`
789	   (`work` -> root, `bot` -> the root-joined `bot` path).
790	4. `-R PATH --scope=ROLES`: roles resolved against `PATH` as the
791	   workspace root.
792	
793	Scope is cwd-portable: from `.claude/`, `vc-x1 sync` walks up to
794	the workspace root and resolves repos by absolute path.
795	
796	| Flag | Description |
797	|------|-------------|
798	| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Workspace root, or a single repo to sync alone. Composes with `--scope` |
799	| `--scope <SCOPE>` | `work|bot|work,bot`: workspace roles to sync. Composes with `-R` |
800	| `-q, --quiet` | Suppress all output; exit code signals result (for scripts) |
801	| `--bookmark <NAME>` | Bookmark to sync in the work repo (bot repo always syncs `main`) [default: main] |
802	| `--remote <NAME>` | Remote to sync against [default: origin] |
803	| `--rebase` | Rebase a non-empty `@` onto the synced bookmark without prompting (work repo only) |
804	
805	**Output shape.** Sync collapses output based on what it finds:
806	
807	- **All up-to-date**: one-line summary,
808	  `sync: N repos are up to date, nothing to sync`. Nothing else
809	  (no-op reposition lines are debug-level).
810	  Makes "sprinkle sync everywhere" genuinely cheap. Scope is
811	  bookmark-vs-remote tracking; `@` may have uncommitted
812	  working-copy changes, and sync intentionally doesn't speak to
813	  that (use `jj st` for working-copy state).
814	- **Action needed** (`behind` / `diverged`): per-repo fetch +
815	  state lines, then the actions run.
816	- **`--quiet`**: no output at any level; exit code is the only
817	  signal. Intended for scripts that just need success/failure.
818	
819	**Note on the `behind` case.** jj's `git fetch` already fast-forwards a
820	tracked local bookmark when it's a strict ancestor of the incoming
821	remote, so in the common case `sync` reports `up-to-date` rather than
822	`behind`. The `behind` branch covers untracked bookmarks and edge
823	configs where auto-advance is disabled.
824	
825	### revert
826	
827	Restore repos to their persisted pre-sync snapshots, the explicit
828	undo completing sync's stop-on-error contract. A failed
829	`vc-x1 sync` leaves each repo's pre-sync `jj op` id in
830	`<repo>/.vc-x1/sync-state.toml`; after inspecting what happened,
831	`vc-x1 revert` runs `jj op restore <op>` in every repo holding a
832	snapshot and clears the consumed state files. Working-copy files
833	are preserved across the restore: jj rewinds the operation log but
834	leaves disk content untouched.
835	
836	Repo set resolution is identical to sync's (`-R` / `--scope` /
837	workspace default), so a failed sync and the following revert name
838	the same repos when invoked the same way. Repos without a snapshot
839	are skipped with a note; sync clears state on success, so that's
840	the normal condition, not an error; finding no snapshot anywhere
841	errors (`nothing to revert`).
842	
843	```
844	vc-x1 sync            # fails: stops, names each repo's pre-sync op id
845	# ...inspect with jj st / jj log / jj op log...
846	vc-x1 revert          # restore every repo to its pre-sync snapshot
847	```
848	
849	| Flag | Description |
850	|------|-------------|
851	| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Workspace root, or a single repo to revert alone. Composes with `--scope` |
852	| `--scope <SCOPE>` | `work|bot|work,bot`: workspace roles to revert. Composes with `-R` |

854	### squash-push
855	
856	Squash `@` into `@-`, advance a bookmark, and push, capturing a
857	repo's trailing working-copy writes and publish them in one step.
858	Rewriting an already-pushed commit this way is a deliberate
859	published-history rewrite, so the push is a forced update.
860	
861	The primary use case is folding the bot repo's session tail: session
862	data keeps landing in `@` after the last commit (including the record
863	of the push itself), and only the user, acting after the bot goes
864	quiet, can capture all of it. Zero ceremony by design:
865	
866	```
867	# In .claude: squash @ -> @-, advance main, push
868	vc-x1 squash-push -R .claude
869	
870	# Bare invocation: same, in the current directory's repo
871	vc-x1 squash-push
872	
873	# Custom bookmark and squash pair
874	vc-x1 squash-push feature -R . --squash @,@--
875	```
876	
877	| Flag | Description |
878	|------|-------------|
879	| `[BOOKMARK]` | Bookmark to advance and push [default: main] |
880	| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Path to jj repo [default: .] |
881	| `--squash [<SOURCE,TARGET>]` | Squash pair [default: @,@-] |
882	
883	Behavior notes:
884	
885	- Runs fully in-process, so a failure is a visible non-zero exit.
886	  (Replaces the `finalize` subcommand, whose detached background
887	  child could be killed silently at command exit.)
888	- With an empty `@` and the bookmark already at the remote it
889	  reports "already sync'd" and exits 0; with an empty `@` but the
890	  remote behind, it skips the squash and still pushes.
891	- If the bookmark doesn't match `BOOKMARK@origin` at start (an
892	  earlier publish was lost; see [validate-bot](#validate-bot)),
893	  it says so and proceeds: publishing is its job.
894	- Preflight refuses bad states before rewriting anything:
895	  unresolvable squash revsets, an ochid-dropping squash (see
896	  [Testing the ochid-trailer guard](#testing-the-ochid-trailer-guard)),
897	  conflicts, a missing / untracked / non-forward bookmark, an
898	  undescribed push target.
899	
900	See [inline session push + squash-push (0.69.0)](./notes/chores/chores-13.md#feat-inline-session-push--squash-push-0690)
901	for design details.
902	
903	### push
904	
905	Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and squash-push
906	the bot repo's `main`: one command with two interactive approval
907	gates. Replaces the old multi-step manual choreography
908	(`jj commit` × 2 -> `jj bookmark set` × 2 -> `jj git push` ->
909	squash-push) with a single invocation.
910	
911	```bash
912	vc-x1 push main                                     # interactive
913	vc-x1 push main --title "..." --body "..."          # skip $EDITOR
914	vc-x1 push main --yes --title "..." --body "..."    # full non-interactive
915	vc-x1 push main --dry-run                           # preview
916	```
917	
918	Stages, top to bottom:
919	
920	| Stage | What it does |
921	|-------|--------------|
922	| `review` | Print `jj diff --stat` for both repos; prompt `[y/N]` (first approval gate) |
923	| `message` | Compose title+body from `--title`/`--body` or an `$EDITOR` template; second approval gate. Skipped when neither repo has pending changes, since a publish-only run needs no message |
924	| `commit-work` | `jj commit` work repo with ochid trailer pointing at `.claude` (skipped when `@` is empty) |
925	| `commit-bot` | `jj commit` `.claude` with ochid trailer pointing at the work repo (skipped if `.claude` is clean) |
926	| `bookmark-set` | `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r @- -R .` and `jj bookmark set main -r @- -R .claude` |
927	| `push-work` | Verify the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, then `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark> -R .` |
928	| `squash-push-bot` | In-process squash of `.claude`'s trailing session writes + push `main` (see [squash-push](#squash-push)) |
929	
930	**Rerunning is always safe.** There is no saved state and no
931	resume: every stage checks its own precondition and does nothing
932	when its work is already done, so re-running after a failure is
933	simply running. A recorded position would describe a world that
934	may have changed for reasons push cannot know. If a run fails,
935	push stops and reports. Please fix and try again.
936	
937	Failures in `commit-work` / `commit-bot` / `bookmark-set` roll
938	both repos back via `jj op restore` to a snapshot taken moments
939	earlier in the same process. Once `push-work` succeeds the work
940	is published: from there a change is either a new commit
941	appended on top by the next push, or an amend of what was
942	pushed, where [`squash-push`](#squash-push) folds the working copy
943	into the last commit and force-updates the remote. See
944	[Recovery](./notes/cycle-protocol.md#recovery).
945	
946	| Flag | Description |
947	|------|-------------|
948	| `[BOOKMARK]` | Work-repo bookmark to advance (the bot repo always advances `main`); positional form of `--bookmark` |
949	| `--bookmark <NAME>` | Same as positional (mutually exclusive) |
950	| `-y, --yes` | Auto-approve both gates (non-interactive use) |
951	| `--title <STR>` / `--body <STR>` | Skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage |
952	| `--dry-run` | Print what would run, no side effects |
953	| `--step` | Pause after every stage for an extra continue-prompt |
954	| `--no-squash-push` | Stop before `squash-push-bot` (run it manually) |
955	
956	See [Add push subcommand (0.37.0)](./notes/chores/chores-05.md#add-push-subcommand-0370)
957	for the full design and [per-step record](./notes/chores/chores-05.md#per-step-record)
958	for what each `0.37.0-N` dev step shipped.

960	### Testing push + squash-push
961	
962	Always test against a throwaway fixture, never the live workspace.
963	Scaffold one with `vc-x1 init <TARGET> --repo local=<PARENT>` (no
964	GitHub, no network), then run the complete flow end-to-end. The
965	work repo uses plain `jj git push`; the bot repo uses
966	`vc-x1 squash-push` to squash trailing writes and push in one shot.
967	
968	`--repo local=<PARENT>` lays out:
969	```
970	<PARENT>/
971	  remote-work.git/     bare git remote for the work repo
972	  remote-bot.git/   bare git remote for the .claude bot repo
973	  <NAME>/              work repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
974	    .vc-config.toml    work="/", bot="/.claude"
975	    .gitignore         /.claude /.git /.jj /target /.vc-x1
976	    .claude/           bot repo (jj colocated, main tracks origin)
977	      .vc-config.toml  work="/", bot="/.claude" (identical)
978	      .gitignore       .git .jj
979	```
980	
981	```bash
982	parent=$(mktemp -u /tmp/vc-x1-test-XXXXXX)
983	vc-x1 init "$parent/work" --repo local="$parent"
984	work="$parent/work"
985	bot="$parent/work/.claude"
986	
987	# 1. work repo: described commit -> advance main -> push
988	echo hello > "$work/hello.txt"
989	jj describe @ -R "$work" -m 'feat: add hello.txt'
990	jj bookmark set main -r @ -R "$work"
991	jj git push -R "$work"
992	
993	# 2. bot repo: trailing writes -> squash-push (fold into @-, push)
994	echo notes > "$bot/notes.md"
995	vc-x1 squash-push -R "$bot"
996	
997	# 3. cleanup when done (init also created a symlink under
998	#    ~/.claude/projects/ pointing at the fixture, remove it too)
999	rm -rf "$parent"
1000	```
1001	
1002	**Why `jj git push` for the work repo but `squash-push` for
1003	`.claude`?** The work repo's workflow is a plain dev commit on `@-`
1004	that we push directly. The bot repo mirrors the bot's runtime
1005	pattern: session writes land in `@` (above the last committed
1006	commit), and squash-push folds those trailing writes into that
1007	commit just before pushing, so one atomic state goes upstream.
1008	
1009	The run is fully in-process and synchronous, so what you see is the
1010	whole flow:
1011	```
1012	$ vc-x1 squash-push -R "$bot"
1013	squash-push: squashing @ -> @-...
1014	squash-push: setting bookmark 'main' to @-...
1015	squash-push: pushing 'main' to origin...
1016	squash-push: done
1017	```
1018	
1019	Preflight failures (bookmark missing, non-tracking remote, squash
1020	revset unresolved, conflicts, push target lacks a description) exit
1021	with a non-zero status and a pointed error on stderr before
1022	anything is rewritten.

1024	### Testing the ochid-trailer guard
1025	
1026	`squash-push` refuses to drop `ochid:` trailers: when the squash
1027	source's message carries trailers the destination's message lacks,
1028	`--use-destination-message` would silently discard them and leave
1029	the counterpart repo's cross-links dangling (the incident is
1030	recorded in
1031	[record finalize ochid-loss bug (0.65.1)](./notes/chores/chores-13.md#docs-record-finalize-ochid-loss-bug-0651)).
1032	The guard
1033	runs in preflight, before anything is rewritten.
1034	
1035	`squash-push` always pushes, so the examples run against a
1036	throwaway init fixture (same shape as
1037	[Testing push + squash-push](#testing-push--squash-push)) using
1038	its bot repo:
1039	
1040	```bash
1041	parent=$(mktemp -u /tmp/vc-x1-guard-XXXXXX)
1042	vc-x1 init "$parent/work" --repo local="$parent"
1043	bot="$parent/work/.claude"
1044	
1045	# example 1, refusal: journal described on @ WITH an ochid
1046	# trailer; squash-push exits 1 naming the trailer
1047	echo b >> "$bot/notes.md"
1048	jj describe -R "$bot" -m 'new journal
1049	
1050	ochid: /abc123abc123'
1051	vc-x1 squash-push -R "$bot"
1052	
1053	# example 2, normal case: clear the description; the squash
1054	# proceeds and the run pushes
1055	jj describe -R "$bot" -m ''
1056	vc-x1 squash-push -R "$bot"
1057	
1058	# cleanup (also remove the fixture's ~/.claude/projects symlink)
1059	rm -rf "$parent"
1060	```
1061	
1062	Output captured from a real run; regenerate these transcripts with
1063	[`support/gen-exmpl-1-3.sh`](support/README.md#gen-example-1---3-output).
1064	Example 1 is refused with exit 1:
1065	
1066	```
1067	$ vc-x1 squash-push -R "$bot"
1068	error: refusing squash @ -> @-: the squash would drop ochid: trailers
1069	the destination's message lacks:
1070	  /abc123abc123
1071	merge the messages by hand (`jj describe @- -R /tmp/vc-x1-guard-hmevVM/work/.claude`) or clear
1072	the source's description, then retry
1073	```
1074	
1075	Example 2 with the description cleared squashes and pushes, exit 0:
1076	
1077	```
1078	$ vc-x1 squash-push -R "$bot"
1079	squash-push: squashing @ -> @-...
1080	squash-push: setting bookmark 'main' to @-...
1081	squash-push: pushing 'main' to origin...
1082	squash-push: done
1083	```
1084	
1085	## Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers
1086	
1087	Commits in each repo use [git trailers](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-interpret-trailers)
1088	to cross-reference their counterpart in the other repo. The `ochid`
1089	(Other Change ID) trailer contains a workspace-root-relative path
1090	and jj changeID:
1091	
1092	```
1093	ochid: /.claude/xvzvruqo   # points to a .claude repo change
1094	ochid: /wtpmottv            # points to an work repo change
1095	```
1096	
1097	Paths always start with `/` (the workspace root, i.e. vc-x1).
1098	Each repo has a `.vc-config.toml` that identifies its location
1099	within the workspace, so tools can resolve these paths locally.
1100	
1101	For full details see:
1102	- [Git trailer convention](./notes/chores/chores-01.md#git-trailer-convention)
1103	  - [ochid (Other Change ID)](./notes/chores/chores-01.md#ochid-other-change-id)
1104	  - [ChangeID path syntax](./notes/chores/chores-01.md#changeid-path-syntax)
1105	  - [.vc-config.toml](./notes/chores/chores-01.md#vc-configtoml)
1106	
1107	## jj Tips for Git Users
1108	
1109	If you're coming from git, jj's log output can be surprising compared to
1110	tools like `gitk --all`.
1111	
1112	### Why `jj log` shows fewer commits than `gitk`
1113	
1114	jj tracks *changes* (identified by change IDs), not individual git commits.
1115	When you rewrite a change (`jj describe`, `jj rebase`, `jj squash`, etc.),
1116	jj creates a new git commit and keeps the old one under `refs/jj/keep/*` as
1117	undo history. `gitk --all` sees all of these obsolete commits; `jj log` only
1118	shows the current version of each change.
1119	
1120	### Useful commands
1121	
1122	| Command | Description |
1123	|---------|-------------|
1124	| `jj log` | Show recent visible commits (default revset) |
1125	| `jj log -r ::@` | Show **all** ancestors of the working copy |
1126	| `jj log -r 'all()'` | Show all non-hidden commits (needed if you have multiple heads/branches) |
1127	| `jj obslog -r <change-id>` | Show the evolution history of a single change |
1128	| `jj op log` | Show operation history (each rewrite operation) |
1129	
1130	In a single-branch workflow, `jj log -r ::@` and `jj log -r 'all()'` give
1131	the same result. Use `all()` when you have multiple branches or heads.
1132	
1133	## Testing
1134	
1135	The repo ships two flavors of tests:
1136	
1137	- **In-process tests**: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { ... }` blocks inside
1138	  `src/*.rs`. These call library code directly (no subprocess spawn)
1139	  and run fastest. The dual / POR fixture tests under
1140	  `src/init.rs::tests` build throwaway workspaces by invoking
1141	  `init::init` as a function.
1142	- **CLI subprocess integration tests**: files under `tests/`. These
1143	  spawn the `vc-x1` binary that Cargo built; its absolute path lives
1144	  in the `CARGO_BIN_EXE_vc-x1` env var that Cargo sets at compile
1145	  time, which `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_vc-x1")` reads and bakes into the
1146	  test binary as a string literal. Argument parsing, exit codes, and
1147	  stdout/stderr are all exercised end-to-end. Each subprocess gets a
1148	  `HOME` override so the user's real `~/.config/vc-x1/` can't leak in
1149	  or get clobbered.
1150	
1151	Run everything with:
1152	
1153	```bash
1154	cargo test                 # unit + integration
1155	cargo test --bins          # binary unit tests only (in-process)
1156	cargo test --test cli_init # one integration test crate
1157	```
1158	
1159	### Test tempdir location
1160	
1161	Both test layers create throwaway fixtures under a tempdir. The
1162	parent directory resolves in priority order:
1163	
1164	1. `$VC_X1_TEST_TMPDIR`: explicit env override.
1165	2. `std::env::temp_dir()`: standard fallback (`$TMPDIR` on Unix,
1166	   else `/tmp`).
1167	
1168	Useful when you want tests on a tmpfs / SSD / project-local path
1169	without exporting `TMPDIR` globally:
1170	
1171	```bash
1172	VC_X1_TEST_TMPDIR=/dev/shm/vc-x1 cargo test
1173	```
1174	
1175	Fixture directories are named `vc-x1-test-<tag>-<ts>-<n>` (in-process)
1176	and `vc-x1-cli-test-<tag>-<ts>-<n>` (CLI). RAII drop removes them on
1177	test exit; SIGKILLs / panics in `Drop` can leak, so search and clean
1178	manually:
1179	
1180	```bash
1181	find "${VC_X1_TEST_TMPDIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}" -maxdepth 1 \
1182	     -name 'vc-x1-*test*' -mtime +1 -exec rm -rf {} +
1183	```
1184	
1185	A future enhancement (tracked in `TODO.md` at the repo root)
1186	extends the priority chain through `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`
1187	and project-local `.vc-config.toml`.
1188	
1189	### Preserving fixtures for debugging
1190	
1191	When a test fails and you want to inspect the workspace it built,
1192	set `$VC_X1_TEST_KEEP`. The RAII `Drop` impls (`Fixture`,
1193	`FixturePor`, `CliFixture`) skip `remove_dir_all` and print the
1194	preserved path on stderr:
1195	
1196	```bash
1197	VC_X1_TEST_KEEP=1 cargo test -- --nocapture 2>&1 | grep TEST_KEEP
1198	```
1199	
1200	Two shell gotchas worth remembering:
1201	
1202	- The preservation message goes to **stderr**, so a plain
1203	  `cargo test | grep ...` won't see it; use `2>&1 |` or write
1204	  the full output to a file.
1205	- `--nocapture` is needed to bypass libtest's stdout/stderr
1206	  capture; without it, the messages get swallowed by the test
1207	  runner's pretty-printer.
1208	
1209	`VC_X1_TEST_KEEP` is a debugging knob: every fixture-creating
1210	test in the run leaks its tempdir while it's set. Clean up with
1211	the `find` recipe above, or just `rm -rf` the announced paths.
1212	
1213	## Support
1214	
1215	Helper scripts for maintaining this repo's docs and examples live
1216	in [`support/`](support/); see
1217	[support/README.md](support/README.md).
1218	
1219	### gen-exmpl-1-3.sh
1220	
1221	Regenerates the captured transcripts for
1222	[Testing the ochid-trailer guard](#testing-the-ochid-trailer-guard)
1223	by running the two examples against a throwaway init fixture and
1224	printing the `$ command` + output blocks ready to paste. Details:
1225	[Gen Example 1 - 3 output](support/README.md#gen-example-1---3-output).
1226	
1227	## Thoughts for the future
1228	
1229	Forward-looking design discussion lives in
1230	[`notes/forks-multi-user.md`](notes/forks-multi-user.md):
1231	forking the dual-repo workspace, multi-user collaboration,
1232	multi-line `ochid:` trailers, bot-repo size and scaling
1233	thresholds, URL-shaped per-user repos for distributed
1234	projects. Treat as a design reference, not a status doc;
1235	most of what's there is forward-looking, not yet
1236	implemented.
1237	
1238	## Contributing
1239	
1240	The tool's internal structure (module map, the CLI-args /
1241	ops-`Context`+`Params` split, the subcommand model, and the
1242	two in-flight migrations) is described in
1243	[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). Start there to orient.
1244	
1245	The bot-facing cycle workflow (cycles for Preparation /
1246	Work / Close-out, per-commit flow with the cargo cycle
1247	`fmt` / `clippy` / `test` / `install`, commit description
1248	shape, ochid trailers, pushing) lives in
1249	[`notes/cycle-protocol.md`](notes/cycle-protocol.md).
1250	
1251	Bot-facing conventions are canonical in
1252	[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (hard rules + file map), its
1253	`agent-data/` satellites, and the project layer
1254	[custom.md](custom.md):
1255	
1256	- [Notes file conventions](agent-data/notes.md):
1257	  Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes references
1258	  (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links,
1259	  Retiring Done entries, and Chores conventions
1260	  (section headers / Done entries exact-title rule,
1261	  content rules, `Commits:` line format).
1262	- [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form): intro +
1263	  bullets shape for long-lived prose (commit bodies,
1264	  chores, doc comments).
1265	- [Code conventions](agent-data/code.md): doc
1266	  comments on every file / fn / method, `// OK: ...` on
1267	  `unwrap*` calls.
1268	
1269	Task tracking and release details: near-term tasks in
1270	[TODO.md](TODO.md), per-release details in

1272	rules in [notes/README.md](notes/README.md).

# vc-x1

- [Overview](#vc-x1)
- [Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md)
- [Terminology](#terminology)
- [Usage](#usage)
  - [Revision shortcuts](#revision-shortcuts)
  - [Shell completion](#shell-completion)
  - [validate-desc](#validate-desc)
  - [fix-desc](#fix-desc)
  - [validate-todo](#validate-todo)
  - [fix-todo](#fix-todo)
  - [validate-bot](#validate-bot)
  - [config](#config)
  - [clone](#clone)
  - [init](#init)
  - [symlink](#symlink)
  - [sync](#sync)
  - [revert](#revert)
  - [squash-push](#squash-push)
  - [push](#push)
  - [Testing push + squash-push](#testing-push--squash-push)
  - [Testing the ochid-trailer guard](#testing-the-ochid-trailer-guard)
- [Cross-repo Linking with Git Trailers](#cross-repo-linking-with-git-trailers)
- [jj Tips for Git Users](#jj-tips-for-git-users)
- [Thoughts for the future](#thoughts-for-the-future)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

This is experiment 1 to explore creating a Vibe Coding (vc) environment.
We will investigate ways of using the dual jj-git repo concept, explored
in [hw-jjg-bot](https://github.com/winksaville/hw-jjg-bot.git) to
initially make it easy to see how the code base evolved. This is
made possible by the fact that we have two repos one with the code
and one with the conversation with the bot.

I've chosen the jj-git environment because jj provides the concept that
each commit has an immutable changeID as well as the mutable commitID
of git. The idea is that each commit made on repo A writes the
changeID in the commit message to repo B. Thus there is a cross reference
between the two repos and this will allow vc-x1 to show how the repo
evolved and the entity (bot or human) can more clearly understand **how** and
most importantly **why** the code evolved.

The solution space is wide open, from trivial CLI, web or app based
(mobile/non-mobile). In addition, I could see this as an extension to
existing programming editors like vscode and zed or even creating our
own IDE for vc.

See [Initial commit with dual jj-git repos](./notes/chores/chores-01.md#initial-commit-with-dual-jj-git-repos)
for how the initial commit was created with the dual jj-git repos. After
doing so and I then created this README.md file.

## Terminology

A vc-x1 workspace pairs two jj-git repos, and this README names
their two sides **work** and **bot**:

- **work repo**: the repo at the project root, holding the work
  product itself (source code, docs, the repo you would have
  anyway).
- **bot repo**: the `.claude` repo nested inside it, holding the
  bot's session data (the conversation that produced the work).
- **work** / **bot**: the two sides as roles, used wherever a
  command or doc needs to say which repo it means (e.g. push's
  `commit-work` / `commit-bot` stages).

A few naming conventions this project keeps, to avoid ambiguous
jargon:

- **path** is reserved for a filesystem location, qualified as
  **relative** or **absolute** when it matters (e.g. `../other`,
  `/home/you/repo`).
- a configuration setting is a **config key**, e.g.
  `bot-session.col-width` (its TOML table and key joined by `.`);
  not a "path".
- a datum in a transcript's `--fields` inventory is a **field**,
  e.g. `message.content[].type`, its levels joined by `.`, with
  `[]` marking array elements.

## Usage

```
vc-x1 list [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # List commits in a jj repo
vc-x1 desc [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # Show full description of a commit
vc-x1 chid [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # Print changeID(s) for a revision
vc-x1 show [-r REVISION] [-n COMMITS]  # Show commit details and diff summary
vc-x1 bot-session <FILE> [OPTS]        # Display a session transcript as a conversation
vc-x1 validate-desc [OPTS]                 # Validate commit descriptions
vc-x1 fix-desc [OPTS]                     # Fix commit descriptions (dry-run default)
vc-x1 validate-todo [FILE]                # Check todo-file entry numbering
vc-x1 fix-todo [FILE]                     # Renumber todo file (dry-run default)
vc-x1 validate-bot [OPTS]                 # Check the bot repo is published
vc-x1 config [OPTS]                       # Print / validate settable config keys
vc-x1 clone <REPO> [NAME] [OPTS]          # Clone a dual-repo project
vc-x1 init <TARGET> [OPTS]                # Create a new dual-repo project
vc-x1 symlink [TARGET] [OPTS]             # Create Claude Code project symlink
vc-x1 sync [OPTS]                          # Fetch + sync both repos to their remotes
vc-x1 revert [OPTS]                        # Restore repos to a prior operation
vc-x1 squash-push [BOOKMARK] [OPTS]        # Squash @ into @-, advance a bookmark, push
vc-x1 push [BOOKMARK] [OPTS]               # Commit both repos, push work, squash-push bot
vc-x1 --version                            # Print version
vc-x1 --help                           # Print help
```

**The `..` notation:** dots on the revision show which direction to
list commits:

- `x..`: x at top, ancestors below (older commits)
- `..x`: descendants above (newer commits), x at bottom
- `..x..`: both directions, x in the middle

COMMITS is the total number of commits to show (x is always included).
Without dots, `x` with a count defaults to `x..` (ancestors).
For `..x..`, the budget is split: ancestors get the extra on odd counts.

```
vc-x1 list -r @              # just @ (1 commit)
vc-x1 list -r @.. -n 5       # @ + 4 ancestors (5 commits, @ at top)
vc-x1 list -r ..@ -n 3       # 2 descendants + @ (3 commits, @ at bottom)
vc-x1 list -r ..@.. -n 3     # 1 descendant, @, 1 ancestor (3 commits)
vc-x1 list -r ..@.. -n 4     # 1 descendant, @, 2 ancestors (4 commits)
```

### Shell completion

vc-x1 provides tab completion for all subcommands and flags using claps
[unstable-dynamic](https://docs.rs/clap_complete/latest/clap_complete/env/struct.CompleteEnv.html)
only feature. It is a "simple" implementation and does not handle completing
revisions but still useful. To enable it, add one of the following to your shell's startup file:

```bash
# bash (~/.bashrc)
source <(COMPLETE=bash vc-x1)

# zsh (~/.zshrc)
source <(COMPLETE=zsh vc-x1)

# fish (~/.config/fish/config.fish)
source (COMPLETE=fish vc-x1 | psub)
```

Completions are generated dynamically by the binary, so they stay in
sync with the installed version automatically.

### Positional shorthand

REVISION and COMMITS can be given as positional arguments, omitting
`-r` and `-n`:

```
vc-x1 list x                # just x (1 commit)
vc-x1 list x 5              # x.. 5 -> x + 4 ancestors (5 commits)
vc-x1 list x.. 5            # same as above
vc-x1 list ..x 3            # 2 descendants + x (3 commits)
vc-x1 list ..x.. 3          # 1 descendant, x, 1 ancestor (3 commits)
vc-x1 list ..x.. 1          # just x (1 commit)
```

**Defaults:** with no arguments, REVISION is `@` and COMMITS is 1
(just the working copy).

Named flags `-r`/`--revision`, `-n`/`--commits`, `-R`/`--repo`, and
`-s`/`--scope` take precedence over positional arguments.

### Multi-repo queries

`-s`/`--scope` selects workspace sides by role keyword; `work` is the
work repo, `bot` is the `.claude` repo, `work,bot` is both. The
workspace root is found by walking up from cwd (the existing
`find_workspace_root` rule).

```
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot          # both sides of the workspace
vc-x1 chid -s work              # just the work repo
vc-x1 chid -s bot               # just the bot repo
vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot    # works with chid / desc / list / show
```

`-R`/`--repo` takes a single path. Used alone it points at one jj
repo (workspace lookup is skipped); combined with `-s` it overrides
the workspace root for the role lookup:

```
vc-x1 chid -R .                  # single repo at .
vc-x1 chid -R .claude            # single repo at .claude
vc-x1 chid -R ../other -s work,bot   # both sides of ../other workspace
```

Defaults preserve prior behavior: no flag -> `[.]`, `-R foo` alone
-> `[foo]`. When multiple repos are resolved (any `-s` that names
more than one role), output is labeled with bold `=== path ===`
headers by default. Control the label with `-l`/`--label` and
`-L`/`--no-label`:

```
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot            # default label: === path ===
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -l "---"   # custom label:  --- path ---
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L         # no label (raw output)
```

Examples:

```
$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot
=== . ===
kwoyvposvsmv

=== .claude ===
zzpksklxyrnw

$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L
kwoyvposvsmv
zzpksklxyrnw

$ vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot
=== . ===
kwoyvposvsmv eae175c3c1b5 (no description set)
pqxtxxpnsmot b0c46930a640 Reorganize notes (0.19.1)
ssokyszzwsxw eeb15bc6d839 Unify .. notation and CLI (0.19.0)

=== .claude ===
zzpksklxyrnw 2388185e42ee (no description set)
tzupykyyvnrp 81ce22e34d41 Reorganize notes (0.19.1)
slmkmroqtqtp 1c33ccaa567d Unify .. notation and CLI (0.19.0)

$ vc-x1 desc -r @- -s work,bot
=== . ===
pqxtxxpnsmot b0c46930a640 Reorganize notes: move older done items to done.md, update todos (0.19.1)

    Move completed items [1]-[13] and their references from todo.md to done.md.
    Replace completed jj-organization todo with new items.

    ochid: tzupykyyvnrp

=== .claude ===
tzupykyyvnrp 81ce22e34d41 Reorganize notes: move older done items to done.md, update todos (0.19.1)

    Session: reviewed and committed notes reorganization for 0.19.1.

    ochid: pqxtxxpnsmot

$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -l "---"
--- . ---
kwoyvposvsmv

--- .claude ---
zzpksklxyrnw
```

Most decoration strings work unquoted (`---`, `===`, `>>>`, `:::`,
`+++`). Use single quotes for strings containing shell metacharacters
like `*`, `!`, `#`, `$`, or `~` (e.g. `-l '***'`). Double quotes
won't protect against `!` (bash history expansion).

With a single repo resolved, no label is printed, backward
compatible with the no-flag default. Multi-repo (`-s work,bot`) is
supported for `chid`, `desc`, `list`, and `show`. `squash-push`
remains single-repo.

`-s` is keyword-only: `work`, `bot`, `work,bot`, `bot,work`.
Path-based single-repo operation uses `-R` (above).

### bot-session

Display a Claude Code session transcript
(`.claude/<uuid>.jsonl`) as a readable conversation. The
transcript format is undocumented and evolves; parsing is
tolerant: unknown entry types are skipped and counted,
malformed lines (e.g. a live session's truncated last line)
warn to stderr and never fail the run.

For what the transcript format looks like (entries, entry
types, the `.`/`[]` field notation) and an example that walks
a small sample through these commands, see
[notes/transcript-format.md](notes/transcript-format.md).

Output is composed of eight **items**, each independently
toggleable:

| Item | Emits | Default |
|------|-------|---------|
| `summary` | trailing stats line (shown / hidden / skipped counts) | on |
| `headers` | `=== role 2026-07-17 04:17:09Z ===` turn headers (UTC) | on |
| `user` | typed user prompts | on |
| `assistant` | assistant reply text | on |
| `tool` | `[tool] Name: gist` call one-liners | on |
| `thinking` | `[thinking]` blocks | off |
| `results` | `[result]` / `[result:error]` lines (capped by `--result-lines`) | off |
| `meta` | meta user lines, `--- system ... ---` lines, sidechain entries | off |

Toggle with `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` (last one wins).
`--all` / `--none` reset the base (every item on / off) and then
per-item flags adjust (`--no-all` and `--no-none` are aliases
of `--none` and `--all`). Bookkeeping line types
(file-history snapshots, progress markers, ...) are never
rendered; they're counted in the summary as "skipped".

Default items resolve git-style, most specific wins:

1. CLI `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` flags
2. workspace `.vc-config.toml`: `[bot-session].items`
3. user `~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`: `[bot-session].items`
4. built-in: `headers,user,assistant,tool,summary`

```toml
# In ~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml (all your workspaces) or
# <workspace>/.vc-config.toml (this workspace, committed):
[bot-session]
items = "headers,user,assistant,tool,summary"
```

```
# Default conversation view
vc-x1 bot-session .claude/<uuid>.jsonl

# Everything: thinking, tool results, meta/system too
vc-x1 bot-session --all FILE

# Prompts only: what was asked, nothing else
vc-x1 bot-session --none --user FILE

# Default view minus tool calls and headers
vc-x1 bot-session --no-tool --no-headers FILE

# Slices by source JSONL line (same unit in every view)
vc-x1 bot-session --lines 40 FILE      # first 40 source lines
vc-x1 bot-session --lines -15 FILE     # last 15 source lines
vc-x1 bot-session --lines 100,20 FILE  # 20 lines from Index 100
vc-x1 bot-session --lines 100,-20 FILE # 20 lines ending at Index 100
vc-x1 bot-session --lines 0 FILE       # stats summary only
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--<item>` / `--no-<item>` | Add / remove one of the eight items (last one wins) |
| `--all` / `--none` | Base: every item on / off (aliases `--no-none` / `--no-all`) |
| `--lines SPEC` | Slice by source JSONL line, 0-based Index (`N` first, `-N` last, `I,C` from I, `I,-C` ending at I; `0` = summary only); the same unit in every view |
| `--result-lines N` | Max lines shown per tool result [default: 10]; `0` = unlimited. Resolves CLI > workspace `.vc-config.toml` `[bot-session].result-lines` > user config > built-in, same as `[bot-session].items` |

Cut points show an `... (N source lines skipped)` marker, and a
sliced run's summary ends with `--lines selected K of M source
lines`; its stats describe only the slice. Timestamps are shown as UTC
(`Z`) exactly when the source timestamp carries it, observed
always, but the format is undocumented, so anything else would
pass through verbatim.

**Alternate views.** The transcript format is undocumented
and evolves, so bot-session doubles as a schema explorer. The
parser keeps every field Anthropic writes while the typed
layer consumes a known subset; the difference is the
unexplored surface:

| Flag | View |
|------|------|
| `--fields` | Field inventory, grouped by each line's `type`: every field observed (e.g. `message.content[].type`, with `.` for nesting and `[]` for array elements) with its count, value kinds, and short samples |
| `--unknown` | Like `--fields`, but only fields the typed layer does not consume: the unmodeled / new surface |
| `--raw` | Pretty-printed source lines (unparseable lines pass through verbatim); no summary or markers |
| `--per-line` | With `--fields`/`--unknown` (implies `--fields`): one fields section per source line instead of aggregating |
| `--col-width N` | First column width in these views [default: 68]; longer field names overflow. Resolves CLI > workspace `.vc-config.toml` `[bot-session].col-width` > user config > built-in, same as `[bot-session].items` |

The default 68 aligns the type column for ~99% of observed field
names; only a tail of `snapshot.trackedFileBackups.<absolute
path>.*` keys, whose embedded absolute paths can be arbitrarily
long, overflow.

`--lines` uses the same source-line unit here, e.g.
`--fields --lines 0,1` inventories just the first line.
`--fields`/`--unknown` ignore item flags; `--raw` conflicts
with them.

```
# What does this format actually contain today?
vc-x1 bot-session --fields FILE

# What don't we model yet / what did Anthropic add?
vc-x1 bot-session --unknown FILE

# Inspect one entry in full (source line 42)
vc-x1 bot-session --raw --lines 42,1 FILE

# Walk a region line by line, fields-table style
vc-x1 bot-session --per-line --lines 40,5 FILE
```

### validate-bot

Check the bot repo is in its expected at-rest state: `main`
matching `main@origin`, with its remote refs tracked. At rest the
two always match, because the bookmark only moves inside a `push` /
`squash-push` run, which publishes it in the same invocation, so
a mismatch means an earlier publish was lost. Read-only and cheap
(two `jj` lookups, no build steps); exits non-zero on any finding
and fixes nothing. Resolve with `vc-x1 squash-push -R <bot-repo>`.

```
# Check ./.claude (run from the project root)
vc-x1 validate-bot

# Explicit bot-repo path
vc-x1 validate-bot -R path/to/.claude
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Path to the bot repo [default: .claude] |

`vc-x1 squash-push` reports the condition and proceeds, since
publishing is its job. `vc-x1 push` no longer checks it: a bot
repo that hasn't been squash-pushed yet isn't a broken state, and
the next push publishes it anyway.

### config

Print the settable config keys for a target config file as an
annotated, commented schema: for each key its description, the
command/context it's `used by`, its default (or a value marked
`# example` when there is no default), and a commented
assignment line ready to paste in. The schema is generated from
one in-code registry, so it can't drift from what the code
actually reads.

- `[TARGET]`: `work`, `bot`, `work,bot` (default), or an
  explicit config-file path. The keywords resolve against the
  surrounding workspace's `.vc-config.toml` files and filter to
  that side's keys; a path carries no side information, so it
  gets the whole schema. The user config
  (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`) has no keyword and is reached
  only by passing its path.
- `--validate`: instead of printing, load the target's actual
  config file(s) and flag any key the schema doesn't recognize
  (a typo, a key in the wrong section, or an unknown key), plus,
  for keyword targets, the legacy-schema rejection and the
  resolved-agreement invariant of a dual workspace's `[repos]`
  registries. Exits non-zero if any problem is found. This is an
  opt-in strict check; a normal config load silently ignores
  unknown keys, for forward-compatibility.

A short sample of the printed schema (workspace home):

```
[bot-session]
# bot-session.col-width — Default --col-width: first-column width in
#   the field-inventory views
#   used by: bot-session --col-width
#   default: 68
# col-width = 68

[repos]
# repos.work — The work repo's path, relative to this config file's
#   directory ("." in the work repo, ".." in the bot repo); the entry
#   resolving to the config's own directory names the side
#   used by: find_workspace_root, side detection (structural; written by init)
#   default: (required — see init)
work = "."   # example
```

A key with no default (`default.account`, in the user home)
instead renders a commented example value:

```
# default.account — Account profile (an [account.<name>] section) to
#   use when --account is absent
#   used by: --account (init and account-aware commands)
#   default: (none)
# account = "work"   # example
```

```
# Print the workspace-settable keys, both sides
vc-x1 config

# Print only the work side's keys
vc-x1 config work

# Print the whole schema for one file (the user config has no
# keyword, reach it by path)
vc-x1 config ~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml

# Check both sides' config files: unknown keys, legacy-schema
# rejection, and the [repos] resolved-agreement invariant
vc-x1 config --validate

# Check one explicit file
vc-x1 config ../other/.vc-config.toml --validate
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `[TARGET]` | `work`, `bot`, `work,bot`, or a config-file path [default: work,bot] |
| `--validate` | Check the target config file(s) instead of printing the schema |

Create a new dual-repo project: a work repo with a `.claude` bot
repo as a git submodule. Both repos are initialized with `git` and `jj`,
configured with `.vc-config.toml`, and pushed to GitHub. The bot
repo is added as a submodule so `git clone --recursive` clones both.

```

# owner/name shorthand, path targets, or a parent directory
vc-x1 init myorg/my-project

# Create private repos
vc-x1 init my-project --private

# Local bare remotes instead of GitHub (offline; used by fixtures)

# Preview without executing

# Seed both repos from template directories (sibling layout)
vc-x1 init my-project --use-template \
    ../vc-x1-work-repo-template,../vc-x1-bot-repo-template

```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `<TARGET>` | URL, owner/name shorthand, path, or bare NAME |
| `[NAME]` | Repo directory name override (URL / owner/name forms only) |
| `--account <NAME>` | Pick `[account.<a>]` from user config |
| `--repo <CAT[=VAL]>` | Repo target, e.g. `local=<PARENT>` for local bare remotes |
| `--por` | Plain single repo (no `.claude/` companion) |
| `--private` | Create private GitHub repos [default: public] |

| `--config <none\|PATH>` | Override the canned `.vc-config.toml` write |

**`--use-template`**. Value is `CODE[,BOT]`. If `BOT` is omitted, defaults
to the sibling directory `<CODE>.claude` (file-name concat, not path
join, since the two templates are not nested). Non-hidden contents are
copied recursively into each target; hidden entries (names starting
with `.`) are skipped since init creates the repo's own hidden files
(`.vc-config.toml`, `.gitignore`, `.git/`, `.jj/`). If either template
has a `README.md` at its root, its first line is rewritten to
`# <repo-name>`: `<name>` for the work repo and `<name>.claude` for
the bot repo. For local verification without hitting GitHub,
combine `--use-template` with `--repo local=<PARENT>`.

skipped under `--repo local=...`).
